367	## The Markdown File (`Test.<ID>.md`)
368	
369	No front matter. Template:
370	
371	```markdown
372	{One-line summary of what the check verifies.}
373	
374	{Rationale: explain WHY this configuration matters for security.}
375	
376	#### Remediation action
377	
378	1. In **Entra ID**, navigate to **{Section}** > **[{Page Name}]({direct admin portal URL})**.
379	2. {Step-by-step instructions to fix the issue.}
380	3. Click **Save**.
381	
382	#### Related links
383	
384	* [{Admin portal link description}]({URL})
385	* [{Benchmark or baseline reference}]({URL})
386	
387	<!--- Results --->
388	%TestResult%
389	```
390	
391	- Exactly one `<!--- Results --->` followed by `%TestResult%`; everything above it is the description.
392	- Do not pass `-Description` to `Add-MtTestResultDetail`, so the `.md` is used.
393	- The `.md` is also shown for rows that did not run (not selected, service not connected), so it must make sense on
394	  its own.
395	- The website page `https://maester.dev/docs/tests/<ID>` is built from this file and the attribute.
396	
397	## Choosing the Attribute Values
398	
399	A built-in check says what it is about, how urgent a failure is and which attack techniques it addresses. Each
400	of those values is chosen with the [attribute rubric](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md).
401	Read the rubric's section for an attribute before you set, change or review its value, and do not take the
402	values of a neighbouring check without checking them against it.
403	
404	| Attribute | The question it answers |
405	| --- | --- |
406	| `Product` | In which product is the fix made? |
407	| `RelatedProduct` | Under which other products would an admin expect to find the check? Optional. |
408	| `Feature` | Which part of the product, a settings page or an object type, is the check about? |
409	| `Area` | Which security theme is it, whatever the product? |
410	| `ResourceType` | What does a failing result point at: the tenant, or a kind of object it lists? |
411	| `Severity` | How much risk does the organization carry while the check fails? |
412	| `UserImpact` | How much does the recommended fix disrupt end users? |
413	| `ImplementationCost` | How much administrator work does the recommended fix take? |
414	| `Mitre` | Which MITRE ATT&CK techniques does the checked control prevent or detect? |
415	| `Control` | Which requirements of CIS, CISA SCuBA, ASD Essential Eight, the ISM or NIST SP 800-53 does a passing result support? |
416	
417	The rubric rates a check by the fix its own `.md` recommends, so write the `.md` before you choose the values.
418	The values of the generated EIDSCA and ORCA checks are in `build/eidsca/eidsca-test-metadata.json` and
419	`build/orca/orca-test-metadata.json`: change a value there and regenerate. The severity of an EIDSCA check is the
420	exception: it comes from the EIDSCA config upstream, so a change to it goes to the EIDSCA repository.
421	
422	### Framework requirements and NIST controls (`Control`)
423	
424	Fill in `Control` on every new check. Do not leave it out because it is optional: decide, and leave it empty
425	only when nothing applies. It is the only way a check is mapped to a framework. Work through these in order:
426	
427	1. **The requirement the check is written for.** A CIS check lists `cis-m365:<id>` or `cis-github:<id>`, a
428	   CISA check lists `cisa-scuba:<id>` and an ASD check `essential-eight:<ISM id>` (or `ism:<ISM id>`), first. If the requirement is not in the suite's framework file yet, add it
429	   there with its facts (level and profiles, or criticality) in the same pull request.
430	2. **A CIS, CISA or ASD requirement that asks for the same setting.** A Maester check that verifies what
431	   `cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1` asks for lists it. A benchmark check never adds its requirement to another suite's
432	   test: when that test already checks what the benchmark asks, the benchmark check is a shim (next section). Look the requirement up in `tests/cis/frameworks/*.json`,
433	   `tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json` and `tests/asd/frameworks/*.json`, or in the lookup of the [test builder](https://maester.dev/test-builder).
434	   `Get-MtTest -Suite CISA | Format-Table Id, Title, Control` shows what the existing checks map to.
435	3. **NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls**, written `nist-800-53-r5:<control>`, chosen with the NIST part of the
436	   rubric's [Control section](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md#control) from the pinned list
437	   `powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json`. At most three, best fit first, and only when a passing result is
438	   direct evidence for the control. Skip this step when step 1 or 2 gave a `cisa-scuba` reference: CISA publishes
439	   the NIST mapping of its policies and the result gets it from the framework file.
440	
441	The first value that names a requirement in a framework file becomes the `Benchmark` of the result, so the order
442	matters. An inventory count, or a health, licensing or tidiness check, usually lists nothing.
443	
444	### A requirement another suite already checks (shims)
445	
446	Benchmarks overlap: CIS, CISA, ASD and Maester tests often read the same setting. Before writing a check for a
447	benchmark requirement, and when reviewing one:
448	
449	1. **Find the tests in every suite that read the setting.** `Get-MtTest -Product <key> -Feature <key> |
450	   Format-Table Id, Title`, and search `tests/` for the Graph endpoint or setting name.
451	2. **Read the benchmark's own sources**, not only the requirement's one-line text: its audit or assessment
452	   guidance and any reference configuration it publishes (CIS audit and remediation sections; the SCuBA baseline
453	   and ScubaGear; for ASD the ISM, the Essential Eight assessment process guide and the ASD Blueprint for Secure
454	   Cloud). Note every concrete value: a number of days, a threshold, a role list, an authentication strength, a
455	   rule that must be Block. Use the web tools; cite the page.
456	3. **Decide:**
457	   - Same check: write a **shim**, a test with its own `Id`, `Title`, `Control`, `Author` and `.md` whose body is
458	     `return <the other test's function>` (`return Test-MtCisMfaForEveryUser`).
459	   - Same check, different value that the other test takes as a parameter: a shim with its own parameter whose
460	     default is the benchmark's value, passed on (`return Test-MtCisSmartLockoutThreshold -MaximumLockoutThreshold $MaximumLockoutThreshold`).
461	   - Something no test checks, or a rule no parameter covers: a check of its own. Read data through
462	     `internal/services/<service>/` helpers, and move a helper there (with a neutral name) when another suite
463	     already has the code; never copy another check's logic or name a generic helper after a suite.
464	
465	A shim declares the same `Product`, `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`,
466	`UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Mitre`, `Service`, `License`, `Permission`, `TenantType`, `Cloud`,
467	`Platform`, `Lifecycle`, `LongRunning` and `Exclusive` as the test it calls; calls a test that is not a shim;
468	passes only parameters that test declares; leaves its own requirement off that test's `Control`; and says in its
469	`.md` what the benchmark asks and which test it runs, by ID. `powershell/tests/general/TestShims.Tests.ps1`
470	enforces all of this. The full guidance, with an example, is
471	[Tests that another suite already has](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx#tests-that-another-suite-already-has).
472	
473	When reviewing, fail a benchmark check that re-implements a check another suite already has when the benchmark's
474	sources give no reason for the difference, and say which test it duplicates and which source you read.
475	
476	### What a benchmark check evaluates
477	
478	A CIS check does what the benchmark's **PowerShell audit procedure** does: the same objects, the same pass
479	condition. When the UI steps and the PowerShell steps differ, follow the PowerShell steps.
480	
481	- **Scope.** The audit reads every object → the check reads every object, including ones that apply to no user
482	  (CIS 6.2.1 checks `AutoForwardingMode` on every `Get-HostedOutboundSpamFilterPolicy` result). The audit reads
483	  one object → the check reads only that one (CIS 2.1.15 uses `-Identity Default`, so no custom policies). Never
484	  narrow a check to the policies users receive, or widen it beyond what the audit reads.
485	- **Values.** Use the thresholds the audit names or its script sets (CIS 2.1.11: 90% of the extension list). Make
486	  one a parameter, defaulting to the benchmark's value, when organizations may need another.
487	- **Missing data.** The object the audit reads is not returned → fail or error, never pass.
488	
489	An effective-policy view belongs in an MT check. For CISA, read the SCuBA baseline and ScubaGear's policy in place
490	of the CIS audit. When reviewing, fail a benchmark check whose scope, values or missing-data handling differ from
491	the audit procedure without a reason from the benchmark, and quote the audit step. The full guidance is
492	[What a benchmark test evaluates](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx#what-a-benchmark-test-evaluates).
493	
494	### Where the keys come from
495	
496	- `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` and `ResourceType` take keys from `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`: the
497	  products with their features, the areas and the resource types. A feature key belongs to one product.
498	- `Product` follows the folder: a check in `tests/maester/entra` or `tests/cisa/entra` is `entra`. The folder map
499	  is in `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestLint.Tests.ps1`; a new service folder needs an entry there.
500	- `Mitre` takes technique IDs from the pinned ATT&CK release, `powershell/assets/MaesterAttackTechniques.json`.
501	  An ID that the release retired or does not know fails the unit tests. Tactics are looked up from the ID and
502	  never typed.
503	- `Control` takes requirement IDs from the framework files (`tests/<suite>/frameworks/<key>.json`) and NIST
504	  control IDs from `powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json`. The unit tests fail on an ID that is in neither.
505	- `Get-MtTest -Product entra -Feature conditional-access | Format-Table Id, Title, Severity, Area, ResourceType`
506	  lists the existing checks of a feature, to compare your values with.
507	- **A new key is added to the taxonomy in the same pull request as the first test that uses it.** Prefer an
508	  existing key. Do not add a key ahead of its test: the unit tests fail on a product, feature, area or resource
509	  type that no test uses. A new area also needs a row in the rubric's area table, which the unit tests compare
510	  with the taxonomy.
511	
512	### Tags
513	
514	`Tag` holds free labels for the owner of a test folder. It is not how Maester classifies a check.
515	
516	- Built-in checks carry no tag for product, feature, area, suite, benchmark, licence, severity or their own ID.
517	  Each of those has an attribute or is derived, and the unit tests fail a built-in check that tags one. Remove
518	  such a tag when you edit an older check.
519	- Do not put `Preview` or `LongRunning` in `Tag`; use `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` and the `LongRunning` flag.
520	- Users select checks with `-Product`, `-Feature`, `-Area`, `-Severity` and `-Suite` on `Invoke-Maester` and
521	  `Get-MtTest`. The tags of Maester 2.x, such as `CA` or `CIS`, still select the checks that carried them, with a
522	  warning, through `powershell/assets/Maester.LegacyTags.json`. That file is generated and never edited, and a
523	  check added after 3.0 is not in it, so do not add a tag to make a new check selectable.
524	- A user's custom test may tag freely.
525	
526	### How the values are checked
527	
528	The unit tests in `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1` check what is mechanical. The
529	`attribute-review` check on the pull request has a reviewer model judge each new or changed value against the
530	rubric. The person or agent who reviews the pull request applies the same rubric. See
531	[How the rubric is enforced](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md#how-the-rubric-is-enforced).
532	
533	When the attribute review fails, change the value, or explain in the pull request why the declared value fits
534	the rubric. When you review a check yourself, follow "Reviewing a test's attributes" in
535	[AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md); it also shows how to run the attribute review before you push.
536	
537	## Step-by-Step Workflow: Creating a New Check
538	
539	1. **Look for a test that already checks it**, in every suite, and for a benchmark requirement read the
540	   benchmark's own sources. If the benchmark asks for what an existing test checks, the new check is a shim; see
541	   [A requirement another suite already checks](#a-requirement-another-suite-already-checks-shims).
542	2. **Reserve an ID.** Check [issue #697](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues/697) and comment to reserve
543	   the next `MT.xxxx` (the maester-issue-manager agent can do this). `Get-MtTest MT.12*` shows which IDs exist.
544	3. **Scaffold** with `New-MtTest -Id <ID> -Title '...' -Service <service> -Product <product key>
545	   -Path ./tests/<suite>/<service>`.
546	4. **Fill in the attribute**: `License`, `Author`, flags as needed.
547	5. **Write the function**: read with `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` or the helpers, decide, `Add-MtTestResultDetail`,
548	   return a boolean. Add parameters for tunable values.
549	6. **Write the guide, the `.md`**, in full: a one-line summary, why the setting matters, numbered remediation
550	   steps with a direct link to the admin portal page, related links (Microsoft Learn, and the benchmark when the
551	   check maps to one), and the results footer. Replace every placeholder that `New-MtTest` wrote; a check with
552	   scaffold text in its guide is not finished. Verify product facts and links with Microsoft Learn.
553	7. **Choose the attribute values** with the rubric: `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `UserImpact`,
554	   `ImplementationCost`, `Mitre`, `Control`, and `RelatedProduct` when one applies. See
555	   [Choosing the attribute values](#choosing-the-attribute-values) and
556	   [Framework requirements and NIST controls](#framework-requirements-and-nist-controls-control). The
557	   [test builder](https://maester.dev/test-builder) shows the allowed values and the rubric for each attribute
558	   and writes the attribute; use it to check a value you are unsure of.
559	8. **Validate offline**: `Import-Module ./powershell/Maester.psd1 -Force; Get-MtTest <ID>` must show
560	   `IsValid = True` and no `Errors`. Name the ID and leave out `-Path`: `Get-MtTest -Path <file>` applies the
561	   rules of a custom test, so it does not report a missing attribute or a key that is not in the taxonomy.
562	9. **Run against a tenant**: `Connect-Maester; Invoke-MtTest -Path <file>` (or `Invoke-MtTest -Id <ID>`). Try
563	   `-Parameter @{...}` for each parameter. Check the row's `Result`, `ReasonCode`, `ResultDetail.TestResult`.
564	10. **Run the unit tests**: `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1`. `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestLint.Tests.ps1`
565	   and `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1` check every built-in test.
566	
567	## Converting a User's Pester-format Test
568	
569	Users' 2.x custom tests (`*.Tests.ps1`) still run when Pester 5.7.1+ is installed. To convert:
570	
571	```powershell
572	Convert-MtTest -Path ./custom -WhatIf
573	Convert-MtTest -Path ./custom | Format-Table Id, Status, Notes
574	```
575	
576	It writes `Test.<ID>.ps1` + `.md` per `It`, turns a `Test-MtConnection` guard into `Service`, removes a blanket
577	`-SkippedBecause Error` catch, and rewrites a trailing `| Should -Be $true` to `return`. The `Describe` name
578	becomes `Feature`, so the row's `Block` stays what it was. The Pester tags are kept in `Tag`, except that a
579	`Preview` tag becomes `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` and a `LongRunning` tag the `LongRunning` flag. Rows marked
580	`NeedsReview` have `TODO` comments; tests with names built at run time are `Skipped` and must be rewritten as
581	families. Once converted, delete the Pester file: the native test runs and the Pester test with the same ID no
582	longer does.
583	
584	A user's custom native test lives in their `custom/` folder, uses their own ID prefix (not `MT.`, `CISA.`, `CIS.`,
585	`EIDSCA.`, `ORCA.`, `AD-`, `AZDO.`, `MT1060.`, or `MP.`, which is reserved for Maester Packs), needs a `.md`, and needs only `Id` and `Title` in its attribute.
586	It may set `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` and `ResourceType` to values of its own (a value that matches the taxonomy
587	is stored as the key), may tag freely and may use `Control`; the rubric applies to it only if its owner wants it
588	to. It can call only Maester's exported commands; to reuse a built-in check it calls `Invoke-MtTest -Id <ID>`.
589	
590	## Validation Checklist
591	
592	### Test logic
593	- [ ] Returns exactly one `$true`/`$false`; no stray pipeline output.
594	- [ ] A benchmark check reads the same objects and uses the same pass condition as the benchmark's PowerShell
595	      audit procedure, and fails or errors when the audited object is not returned.
596	- [ ] No other suite already checks the same setting; or the benchmark's own sources were read and the check is
597	      a shim of that test, or differs from it for a reason those sources give.
598	- [ ] No `Test-MtConnection` guard, no `Get-MtLicenseInformation` check; `Service` and `License` declared instead.
599	- [ ] No blanket `try { } catch { Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Error ... }`.
600	- [ ] `-SkippedBecause NotApplicable` (not `$null`) when the check does not apply.
601	- [ ] Data retrieval uses `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` or Maester helpers.
602	- [ ] No hard-coded GUIDs, tenant IDs or names; tunables are described parameters.
603	- [ ] No writes to `$script:`, `$global:`, `$env:` or `$__MtSession`.
604	- [ ] `Platform = 'Windows'` if it uses Windows-only commands.
605	
606	### Attribute and files
607	- [ ] `Test.<Id>.ps1` and `Test.<Id>.md` in the right suite folder; ID unique and not reused.
608	- [ ] `Id`, `Title`, `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `Mitre`, `Service`, `Author` set;
609	      values constant.
610	- [ ] `UserImpact` and `ImplementationCost` set, or both left out when `Severity` is `Info`.
611	- [ ] `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` and `ResourceType` are keys from `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`; a
612	      new key is added there in this pull request.
613	- [ ] Each of those values, and `RelatedProduct` if set, checked against its section of the
614	      [attribute rubric](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md), with the reason visible in
615	      the description or the remediation text.
616	- [ ] No `Category` or `Preview`; no `Tag` for product, feature, area, suite, benchmark, licence,
617	      severity or the ID. `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` and the `LongRunning` flag where they apply.
618	- [ ] A CIS, CISA or ASD check sets `Control` to its requirement (`cis-m365:<id>`, `cis-github:<id>`, `essential-eight:<id>` or
619	      `cisa-scuba:<id>`), first, and the requirement is in the suite's framework file.
620	- [ ] `Control` was considered for every check: a CIS or CISA requirement that asks for the same setting, and
621	      NIST SP 800-53 controls from `powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json` (none when a `cisa-scuba`
622	      reference already brings them). Left empty only when nothing applies.
623	- [ ] `[CmdletBinding()]` and `[OutputType([bool])]`; comment-based help inside the function.
624	- [ ] `Get-MtTest <ID>` (without `-Path`) reports no errors.
625	
626	### Documentation
627	- [ ] `.md` has summary, rationale, `#### Remediation action` with portal links, and ends with `<!--- Results --->` + `%TestResult%`.
628	- [ ] No scaffold placeholder is left in the `.md` ("Describe what this test checks", "Explain how to fix"), and its links open the page they name.
629	- [ ] Pass message starts with "Well done."; fail message is actionable.
630	
631	### Code style
632	- [ ] One True Brace Style; Pascal Case; full cmdlet names (no aliases); 4-space indentation.
633	- [ ] UTF-8 with BOM for `.ps1` files.
634	
635	### Pre-pull request
636	- [ ] `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` passes (PSScriptAnalyzer included).
637	- [ ] Ran against a tenant with `Invoke-MtTest`.
638	- [ ] Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/).
639	
640	## Common Mistakes
641	
642	| Mistake | Why it matters | Fix |
643	| --- | --- | --- |
644	| Adding a `Test-MtConnection` guard or licence check | Duplicates the engine's gate; lint fails | Declare `Service` / `License` |
645	| Wrapping the body in `try`/`catch` that reports `-SkippedBecause Error` | Lint fails; the engine already does it | Remove it; catch only specific conditions |
646	| Returning `$null` for "not applicable" | Reported as `Skipped`/`NoResult` | `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotApplicable` |
647	| Uncaptured output (`$list.Add(...)`) | `Error`/`InvalidReturn` | `$null = $list.Add(...)` |
648	| Variables or `@()` in the attribute | `InvalidMetadata` | Constants and `('a', 'b')` lists only |
649	| `Category` or `Preview` in the attribute | `InvalidMetadata`; both were removed in 3.0 | `Product` and `Feature`; `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` |
650	| A `Tag` such as `'CA'`, `'Entra'` or `'Maester'` on a built-in check | Unit tests fail; tags are not the taxonomy | Use the attribute that says it; see [Tags](#tags) |
651	| A product alias (`'Entra ID'`) or a key that is not in the taxonomy | Unit tests fail | Use the key from `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`, or add the key in the same pull request |
652	| Re-implementing a check another suite already has | Two tests give two answers for one setting and drift apart with every benchmark update | A shim that returns the other test's result; see [shims](#a-requirement-another-suite-already-checks-shims) |
653	| A generic helper named after a suite (`Get-MtAsd*`) in `internal/checks/<suite>/` | Other suites copy it instead of reusing it | A neutral name in `internal/services/<service>/` |
654	| Copying `Severity`, `Area` or `Mitre` from a similar check | The value may not fit this check, and the attribute review fails a value that does not fit | Choose each value with the rubric |
655	| Validating a built-in check with `Get-MtTest -Path` only | It applies the rules of a custom test and reports no missing attribute | `Get-MtTest <ID>` |
656	| File name does not match `Id` | `InvalidMetadata` | Rename to `Test.<Id>.ps1` |
657	| Missing `[CmdletBinding()]` | `InvalidMetadata` | Add it before `param()` |
658	| Hard-coded thresholds or object IDs | Users cannot tune the check | Make them described parameters |
659	| Multi-line `#` comment above a parameter | Only the last line is read as its description | One-line comment or `.PARAMETER` |
660	| `Invoke-MgGraphRequest` / `Get-Mg*` | Bypasses caching | `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` |
661	| Using `-Severity` or `-TestTitle` on `Add-MtTestResultDetail` | Ignored for single-result checks | Set them in the attribute |
662	| Editing generated EIDSCA/ORCA files | Overwritten | Change the generator or the test files |
663	| Adding the function to `FunctionsToExport` | Check functions are internal in 3.0 | Don't |
664	| Missing `%TestResult%` in `-Result` with `-GraphObjects` | The object table is not inserted | Include the placeholder |
665	
666	## Reference Examples
667	
668	- `tests/maester/entra/Test.MT.1012.ps1` + `.md` -- simple Graph check with a licence gate.
669	- `tests/maester/entra/Test.MT.1198.ps1` -- check with a `ValidateRange` parameter, `LongRunning`.
670	- `tests/maester/drift/Test.MT.1060.ps1` -- family with `InstanceSource` and `$Instance`, `Service = 'None'`.
671	- `tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.3.5.ps1` -- CISA check.
672	- `tests/cisa/exchange/Test.CISA.MS.EXO.14.1.ps1` -- check with a `RelatedProduct`.
673	- `tests/maester/azure-devops/Test.AZDO.1045.ps1` -- `Info` check with `Mitre = 'None'` and `Lifecycle = 'Preview'`.
674	- `tests/eidsca/Test.EIDSCA.AF01.ps1` -- generated thin check comparing a tenant value.
675	- `tests/orca/Test.ORCA.100.ps1` -- generated ORCA check.
676	- `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx` -- the full native test guide.
677	- `website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md` -- how to choose each attribute value.
678	- `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1` -- the product, feature, area and resource type keys.
679	- `website/docs/configuration/applicability.mdx` -- gate order and reason codes.
680	
681	## Troubleshooting
682	
683	| Symptom | Likely cause | Resolution |
684	| --- | --- | --- |
685	| `Error` / `InvalidMetadata` | Attribute or file rule broken | `Get-MtTest <ID>` lists each problem with its line (`Get-MtTest -Path <file>` for a custom test) |
686	| Attribute review fails on the pull request | A value does not fit the rubric | Change it to the expected value, or explain in the pull request why the declared value fits |
687	| `Error` / `InvalidReturn` | Non-boolean or multiple outputs | Capture stray output; return one boolean |
688	| `Error` / `InvalidConfiguration` | Bad parameter value in config or `-Parameter` | Check `Get-MtTest <ID>` parameters; fix the value |
689	| `Error` / `TestError` | Exception in the body (often a permission) | Read `ReasonDetail` / `ErrorRecord` |
690	| `Skipped` / `ServiceNotConnected` | Declared service not connected | `Connect-Maester -Service <service>` |
691	| `Skipped` / `LicenseNotFound` | Tenant lacks every `License` element | Expected; check the token |
692	| `Skipped` / `NoResult` | Returned `$null` | Return a boolean or skip explicitly |
693	| `NotRun` / `LongRunning` or `Preview` | Excluded by default | `-IncludeLongRunning` / `-IncludePreview`, or `Invoke-MtTest -Id` |
694	| `NotRun` / `OptInServiceNotConnected` | Active Directory check without AD connection | `Connect-Maester -Service ActiveDirectory` |
695	| Report shows no description | `.md` missing, misnamed, or `-Description` passed | Name it `Test.<ID>.md`; drop `-Description` |
696	| `%TestResult%` appears literally | Placeholder missing from `-Result` with `-GraphObjects` | Add it |
697	| 403 from Graph | Missing scope | Add it to `Get-MtGraphScope` |

content.content:
---
title: Attribute rubric
description: How to choose the classification, priority and mapping attributes of a Maester test, and how those choices are checked.
sidebar:
  order: 2
---

# Attribute rubric

Every test shipped with Maester declares what it is about, how urgent a failure is and which attack techniques
it addresses. This page is the rule book for those values. Unit tests check what can be checked mechanically, and
a review step checks the judgement calls against this page. A custom test may use the same attributes; the rules
apply to it only if you want them to.

The [test builder](/test-builder) lets you pick the values with this guidance beside each field and
shows the code as you go.

| Question | Attributes | Required for built-in tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What is it about? | `Product`, `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType` | All except `RelatedProduct` |
| What do I fix first? | `Severity`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost` | `Severity` always. The other two unless `Severity` is `Info` |
| What does it map to? | `Mitre`, `Control` | `Mitre` (technique IDs or `None`) |
| Is it current? | `Lifecycle`, `ReplacedBy` | No. `Lifecycle` defaults to `Stable` |

The allowed keys for `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` and `ResourceType` are in
[`powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1).
Add a key there in the same pull request as the first test that needs it.

## Rate the test, not your tenant

Rate every value for a typical organization that fails the test, using the fix the test's own Markdown file
recommends. Do not rate for the best case, the worst case or one tenant you know. When two values fit, choose the
lower one for `Severity`, `UserImpact` and `ImplementationCost`. A reader should be able to see the reason for
each value in the test's description and remediation text.

## Product

The product where the fix is made. One value.

- Use the product whose admin surface holds the setting, not every product the test reads from.
- Tests in a product folder (`tests/maester/entra`, `tests/cisa/exchange`) use that folder's product.
- A product the test only reads from, or a licence it needs, is not a second product. `Service` and `License`
  already say that.

## RelatedProduct

Other products the test also checks or depends on. Optional list, never the same key as `Product`.

- Add one when an admin of that product would expect to find the test under it. An Exchange Online test about an
  anti-phishing policy that is managed in the Defender portal has `RelatedProduct = 'defender'`.
- Add one when the fix is made in that product's portal although the test lives in another product's folder.
- Do not add a product only because its API is called.

## Feature

The part of the product the test is about. One key from the product's `Features` list.

- Choose the feature whose settings page or object type the remediation sends the admin to.
- When a test spans two features, choose the one that fails most directly. A Conditional Access policy that
  requires a compliant device is `conditional-access`, not `devices`.
- Tests that check the same thing get the same feature, whatever folder or suite they are in.
- A feature that would hold one test only is usually too narrow. Prefer an existing feature.

## Area

The security theme, whatever the product. One key.

| Key | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `authentication` | How an identity proves who it is: MFA, authentication methods, passwords, legacy protocols, Kerberos and NTLM hardening, session and token lifetime. |
| `privileged-access` | Administrative roles and accounts: who holds them, just-in-time elevation, emergency access, admin tiering, delegated admin rights. |
| `access-control` | Who may reach which resource under which conditions: device, location and risk conditions, permissions on objects, user defaults. |
| `applications` | App registrations, service principals and their credentials, consent and API permissions, OAuth apps, add-ins, connectors. |
| `external-access` | Guests, cross-tenant access, federation and trusts, external sharing and external communication. |
| `devices` | Device compliance, enrollment and configuration, endpoint protection, device identity. |
| `email-protection` | Anti-phishing, anti-spam and anti-malware, Safe Links and Safe Attachments, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, mail flow rules, meeting and messaging protections. |
| `data-protection` | Data loss prevention, sensitivity labels, encryption, retention, backup. |
| `logging-and-detection` | Audit logs, diagnostic settings, alert policies, sensors and the health of detection tooling. |
| `identity-lifecycle` | Stale and dormant accounts, ownership, access reviews, entitlement management, group membership hygiene. |
| `infrastructure` | The directory and platform itself: domain controllers, DNS, replication, sites, schema, Group Policy health, protocol hardening, subscriptions, tenant-wide platform settings. |
| `engineering-systems` | DevOps organizations, repositories, pipelines, build identities, the software supply chain. |
| `ai` | AI agents and copilots: who can use and share them, how they authenticate, what data and tools they reach. |

When more than one area fits, choose by what the control is for, in this order:

1. It protects administrators or admin rights: `privileged-access`.
2. It decides how sign-in is proven: `authentication`.
3. It is about an application, service principal or agent as the subject: `applications`, or `ai` for agents.
4. It is about people or data outside the organization: `external-access`.
5. Otherwise the area that names the mechanism: `access-control`, `devices`, `email-protection`,
   `data-protection`, `logging-and-detection`, `identity-lifecycle`, `engineering-systems`, `infrastructure`.

A product never decides the area on its own. An Azure DevOps test about who is a Project Collection Administrator
is `privileged-access`, not `engineering-systems`.

Inventory and health tests with no security theme of their own are `infrastructure`. When no area fits, choose
the closest and say so in the pull request, so the list can be reviewed.

## ResourceType

What a failing result points at. One key.

- `Tenant` when the test evaluates one tenant-, organization-, forest- or domain-wide setting. The result is
  about the environment.
- `Tenant` when the test checks that at least one policy of a kind exists, even when it lists the policies that
  satisfy it. A failing result has nothing to list.
- `Tenant` when the test evaluates the single default or global policy of a kind, because there is one of it and
  it applies to everyone.
- Otherwise the kind of object a failing result lists or counts: `User`, `Application`, `Device`,
  `ConditionalAccessPolicy`, `GroupPolicy` and so on. A test that evaluates every policy and lists the ones that
  fail uses the policy type.
- A test that counts objects for review (an inventory test) uses the type it counts. When no key names that kind
  of object and it is a one-off, use `Tenant`.
- A family test, which yields one result per instance, uses the type of the instance.

## Severity

The risk to the organization while the test fails. Not the effort to fix it and not the disruption of fixing it.

| Value | A failing result means |
| --- | --- |
| `Critical` | An attacker with no special position can take over the tenant, the domain or a privileged identity, or a secret is already exposed. Directly exploitable and wide in reach. |
| `High` | A primary control is missing or weakened for many users or for privileged identities, and common techniques such as phishing, password spray or consent phishing are enough to use it. |
| `Medium` | A defence-in-depth control is missing, or the exposure is limited to a few objects or one workload, or using it needs another weakness first. |
| `Low` | Hardening or hygiene with a small security effect on its own. |
| `Info` | The test reports a fact for review and makes no risk judgement. Info tests are left out of scores. |

Decide in this order:

1. **Reach.** Privileged identities or the whole tenant move the value up. A single workload or a few objects
   move it down.
2. **Directness.** Usable from the internet or by any signed-in user moves it up. Needing an earlier compromise
   moves it down. A password taken by phishing, spray or stuffing is not an earlier compromise: those are the
   common techniques `High` already assumes.
3. **Role of the control.** The main control for a threat rates higher than a second layer behind another control.

`Critical` is rare. If the description cannot say in one sentence how an attacker gets from the failing state to
admin rights or exposed secrets, the value is `High` or lower. A benchmark's own wording does not set the value:
a SHALL policy can be `Medium`.

Five cases come up often:

- **A test that passes whenever its data can be read** is `Info`, whatever the data is about. If the fact
  deserves a severity, the test should fail on it.
- **A failure that is only an outage or untidiness**, such as replication health, an expiring token or an unused
  object, is `Low`. It is `Medium` or higher only when the outage switches off a security control, and then it is
  rated as the loss of that control.
- **Alerts and notifications** are a second layer behind the control they watch, so they are `Medium` at most.
- **The same check in two suites** gets the same value in both. Usually the second is a shim that returns the
  first test's result and declares all of its values; see
  [Tests that another suite already has](./index.mdx#tests-that-another-suite-already-has).
- **The main control against an attack that starts from a stolen password** is `High`. A second layer behind
  that control is `Medium`. Number matching against MFA fatigue is `High`; showing the app name and location in
  the prompt is `Medium`.

Anchors from existing tests:

| Test | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No Group Policy object contains a `cpassword` | `Critical` | Any domain user can read and decrypt the stored password. |
| No domain admin account has a service principal name | `Critical` | Any domain user can request a ticket and crack an admin password offline. |
| Legacy authentication is blocked | `High` | Password spray bypasses MFA for every user. |
| Number matching is required for Authenticator push notifications | `High` | MFA fatigue works against any user once a password is phished. |
| Authenticator shows the app name and location | `Medium` | A second layer behind number matching. |
| Users cannot register applications | `Medium` | Needs a signed-in user and a further step to cause harm. |
| MailTips are enabled for end users | `Low` | A small aid against mis-sent mail. |
| Disabled user count should be retrievable | `Info` | Inventory for review. |
| [EIDSCA.AP14 — users may read other users](/docs/tests/EIDSCA.AP14) | `Info` | Disabling `allowedToReadOtherUsers` is not itself a security finding. Review the restriction because it can disrupt collaboration, user lookup and default features. |

Microsoft's [Zero Trust Assessment](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment) rates many of the same
Microsoft Entra and Intune settings. Where it has a test for the same setting, compare your value with its risk
level and give the reason in the pull request if the two differ.

## UserImpact

How much the recommended fix disrupts end users. Administrators and the owners of applications are not end
users here. Developers are the end users of Azure DevOps and GitHub.

| Value | Applying the fix |
| --- | --- |
| `Low` | End users notice nothing, or only administrators are affected. |
| `Medium` | Some users change how they work or meet a new prompt: a group loses a capability, users register a method once, a legacy client stops working for a subset. |
| `High` | Most users change a daily habit, or a mistake locks people out or stops mail or an app for many. Needs communication and a staged rollout. |

Omit `UserImpact` when `Severity` is `Info`.

## ImplementationCost

How much administrator work the recommended fix takes.

| Value | The fix is |
| --- | --- |
| `Low` | One setting or one policy in one portal. Under an hour, with no dependency on another team, a licence purchase or a rollout. |
| `Medium` | Several steps: a policy that needs exclusions and a pilot, clean-up of a handful of objects, coordination with one other team. Hours to a few days. |
| `High` | A project: new licences, infrastructure or process, a migration of users or apps, or clean-up across many objects. Weeks or more. |

Clean-up that one administrator can finish alone in a sitting is `Low`. Clean-up that needs the owner of each
object is `Medium`. Turning on a plan that is billed by use is `Medium`: the click is easy, the budget approval is
not. Count the work of the fix, including exclusions and rollout, but not the time to decide.

Omit `ImplementationCost` when `Severity` is `Info`.

## Mitre

The MITRE ATT&CK techniques that the checked control prevents or detects. A list of technique IDs, or `None`.

- IDs only, in the form `T1110` or `T1110.003`. Tactic names are looked up from the pinned ATT&CK release
  (`powershell/assets/MaesterAttackTechniques.json`) and are never typed.
- Use a sub-technique when the control addresses only that sub-technique. When three or more sub-techniques of
  one technique apply, list the technique instead. Do not list a technique together with one of its own
  sub-techniques.
- List a technique only if the test's description explains, or plainly implies, how the control stops or reveals
  it. At most five.
- A test that implements a benchmark which publishes a mapping, such as CISA SCuBA, starts from that mapping and
  then applies these rules. An ID the pinned release has retired is replaced by its successor in that release,
  found by name.
- The description means the comment-based help and the Markdown file together.
- Use `None` for a test with no attacker behaviour behind it, such as replication health or an inventory count.
  An inventory test lists a technique only when the fact it reports is itself the precondition of that technique,
  such as accounts that do not require Kerberos pre-authentication.
- A retired or unknown ID fails the unit tests.

## Control

Requirements of frameworks the test implements or supports, written `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>`, for
example `cis-m365:5.1.5.1`, `cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1` or `nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)`. Optional list. Any test can use
it: one shipped with Maester or one of your own.

- `Control` is the only way a test is mapped to a framework. A CIS test carries `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'` and
  a CISA test carries `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'` and an ASD test `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'`.
  Every test in `tests/cis`, `tests/cisa`, `tests/asd` and `tests/disa` must name a requirement of its suite's framework. The unit
  tests check this.
- The first value that names a requirement in a framework file becomes the `Benchmark` of the result. Put the
  requirement the test is written for first, and any other requirement it supports after it.
- Use the same attribute for a test that exists for its own reasons and also supports a requirement: a Maester
  test that checks the setting a CISA policy asks for, or a CIS test that also supports a NIST control.
- When the key is a framework shipped with Maester (`cis-m365`, `cis-github`, `cisa-scuba`, `essential-eight`, `ism`), the requirement must
  exist in that framework's file. If it is new, add it to the file with its facts. The module build and the unit
  tests fail otherwise.
- Do not repeat the `Related` controls of a requirement. The framework file lists them and Maester adds them to
  the result.
- List a requirement only when a passing result is evidence for it. A test that checks one part of a requirement
  may list it; a test that is merely on the same topic may not.

A reference says the test supports the requirement. It never says the organization complies with it.

### NIST SP 800-53

A test may list the NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls its setting implements, as `nist-800-53-r5:<control>`.

- Use an ID from the pinned list, [`powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json):
  a base control (`AC-2`) or an enhancement (`IA-2(1)`). The unit tests reject anything else.
- List a control only when a passing result is direct evidence that it is implemented for what the test checks.
- Prefer the enhancement when the test checks exactly what it says: MFA for privileged accounts is `IA-2(1)`.
  Do not list a base control together with one of its own enhancements.
- At most three, best fit first. Never the policy-and-procedures controls (`AC-1`, `IA-1` and so on).
- A test that only reports a count, or checks health, licensing or tidiness, lists none, unless the count is
  itself what a control asks to be tracked: dormant accounts for `AC-2(3)`.
- A test that implements a CISA SCuBA policy does not list NIST controls. CISA publishes that mapping, the
  framework file carries it as `Related`, and the result gets it from there.

## Lifecycle and ReplacedBy

- `Preview`: new and still changing. Not run unless previews are included.
- `Stable`: the default.
- `Deprecated`: kept so history stays readable. Give `ReplacedBy` when another test took its place.

## Tag

`Tag` holds labels the owner of a test folder finds useful. It is not part of Maester's taxonomy.

- Built-in tests do not carry tags for product, feature, area, suite, benchmark, licence, severity or their own ID.
  Each of those has an attribute or is derived.
- A custom test may tag freely.

## Parameter names

A parameter's name is what an administrator types in `TestSettings` and reads in `Get-MtTest` and the results, so
every parameter of a test shipped with Maester follows one convention. A name belongs to its own test: two tests
may use one name for two different things, and nothing links them unless both bind the same setting. Still, a
name says what is measured, so a reader never has to open the test to learn what a value means.

| Kind of value | Name | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upper or lower limit | `Maximum` or `Minimum`, what is measured, then the unit | `MaximumInactiveDays`, `MinimumPasswordLength`, `MaximumIdleTimeoutMinutes` |
| Other number of days, hours or minutes | What it is, then the unit | `ExpiringWithinDays`, `EvaluationPeriodDays` |
| List | Its role, then a plural noun | `ExcludedGroups`, `AllowedPolicies`, `ParkedDomains` |
| Switch | What turning it on does; off by default | `Strict`, `AllDevices`, `SkipHybridJoinCheck` |
| Choice | A noun for what is chosen, with a `ValidateSet` | `PolicyFiltering`, `ComplianceLogic` |

- PascalCase. Spell out `Maximum` and `Minimum`, never `Max` or `Min`.
- A unit is a plain suffix: `Days`, `Hours`, `Minutes`, `Seconds`. Not `InDays`.
- A `string[]` or `object[]` name is plural.
- Say what is measured. `MaximumInactiveDays`, not `ThresholdDays`; `MaximumValidationAgeDays`, not
  `StaleThresholdDays`.
- Reuse an established name for the same idea. If other tests already call it `MaximumInactiveDays`, a new test
  that counts days without a sign-in does not call it `DormantDays`.
- Do not use the names of PowerShell common parameters (`Force`, `Confirm`, `WhatIf`, `PassThru`).

### Parameters bound to a setting

A fact about the tenant or a choice the organisation makes once, such as its parked domains or its emergency
access accounts, is a setting in `GlobalSettings`. A test receives it as a parameter bound to that setting:

```powershell
param(
    # Domains that never send email.
    [MaesterParameter(Setting = 'ParkedDomains')]
    [string[]] $ParkedDomains = @()
)
```

- Bind a parameter only when the value means the same thing to every test that binds it, and the organisation
  sets it once. A value a benchmark sets, such as a lockout threshold, is never bound: each benchmark test keeps
  its own default.
- A test never calls `Get-MtSetting` for such a value. The engine binds it, so `Get-MtTest` and the results show
  it and a `TestSettings` row can override it.
- A setting is named after what it holds, never after a test or a suite. It is registered in
  `powershell/assets/MaesterSettings.psd1` with its type, default, allowed values and, for a list of objects,
  the properties of an item; a pack names its own settings `Namespace.Key` and declares them under `Settings`
  in its `maester-pack.json`.
- The parameter's type, default and `ValidateSet` are those of the setting. The config is checked against the
  registry once before a run, so a test must not accept or default to anything else.
- Pass the value to the helpers that need it. A helper never reads a setting that tests bind, or it would ignore
  the value the test was given.
- A shim declares each bound parameter of the test it calls and passes it on. The engine binds the parameters of
  the test it runs, the shim; the function the shim calls is an ordinary call.
- A connection or transport setting that a connect command or a data helper needs, such as `GitHubOrganization`
  or `XspmExternalDataUris`, is not a test input and is read with `Get-MtSetting`. It is still registered, and
  the engine records the read on the result of the test that caused it (`SettingsRead`).

## How the rubric is enforced

1. **Unit tests** (`powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1` and
   `powershell/tests/general/TestParameterNames.Tests.ps1`) fail when a built-in test misses a
   required attribute, uses a key that is not in the taxonomy, pairs a feature with the wrong product, lists a
   retired ATT&CK technique, carries a taxonomy tag, names a requirement that a shipped framework file does not
   have, or is a CIS or CISA test without a `Control` for its own framework. They also fail on a parameter name
   that breaks a mechanical rule of [Parameter names](#parameter-names): not PascalCase, `Max` or `Min`, a unit
   with `In`, a singular list, a common parameter's name, one name with two types, or a bound parameter whose default or
   allowed values differ from its setting. And they fail when a built-in test calls `Get-MtSetting`, a helper
   reads a setting that tests bind, the module or a shipped pack reads a setting that is not declared, or a shim
   does not pass on a bound parameter of the test it calls (`powershell/tests/general/TestShims.Tests.ps1`).
2. **Attribute review** runs on every pull request that adds a test or changes one of these attributes. A
   reviewer model reads the test, its Markdown file and this page, and fails the check when a value does not fit
   the rubric, with the value it expected and the reason. It also sees the attributes of the other tests with the
   same product and feature. It fails a test whose area, resource type or severity differs from the same check in
   another suite, and whose user impact or implementation cost differs when both plainly recommend the same fix.
   MITRE techniques and related products are not compared. It also reviews the names of a new, renamed or
   rebound parameter against [Parameter names](#parameter-names) and the names other tests already use. A
   maintainer can overrule it.
3. **Reviewers**, human or agent, apply the same page. See `AGENTS.md`.

﻿function Test-MtAsdJustInTimeAdministration {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that privileged directory roles are activated when needed and not assigned, so that administration is just-in-time.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1649 (Essential Eight, Restrict administrative privileges, Maturity Level Three) asks that just-in-time
    administration is used for the administration of systems and their resources. ASD's assessment guide says
    privileged users are granted access "immediately before that access is required and for only as long as it
    is required", and the ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud makes every Microsoft Entra role an eligible assignment,
    with permanent active assignments only for break glass accounts. That is what CIS.M365.5.3.1 checks: an
    active assignment that was not made by an activation fails, whether or not it has an end date. This test
    runs that check (Test-MtCisPrivilegedRolesActivatedNotAssigned).

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdJustInTimeAdministration

    Returns true when every active assignment to a privileged role was made by an activation, apart from the emergency access accounts.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1649
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1649',
        Title = 'Just-in-time administration is used for the administration of systems and their resources.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'privileged-identity-management',
        Area = 'privileged-access',
        ResourceType = 'DirectoryRole',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre = ('T1078.004', 'T1098.003'),
        Control = ('essential-eight:ISM-1649', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-2(7)', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-6(5)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = ('AAD_PREMIUM_P2', 'Entra_Identity_Governance'),
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Emergency access (break glass) accounts and groups, from the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting.
        [MaesterParameter(Setting = 'EmergencyAccessAccounts')]
        [object[]] $EmergencyAccessAccounts = @()
    )

    return Test-MtCisPrivilegedRolesActivatedNotAssigned -EmergencyAccessAccounts $EmergencyAccessAccounts
}

content.content:
## Files and layout

Put your tests in a folder of your own, usually `custom/` inside the folder you run Maester from:

```text
maester/
  maester-config.json        (optional: your run configuration)
  custom/
    Test.CONTOSO.1001.ps1
    Test.CONTOSO.1001.md
    suite.json               (optional: name, tags and source for every test in the folder)
    maester-config.json      (optional: an overlay on the root config)
```

`Invoke-Maester -Path ./maester` finds every `Test.*.ps1` file under the path, in any subfolder up to three
levels deep (`./maester/a/b/c/Test.CONTOSO.1001.ps1`). If you leave out `-Path`, Maester looks for custom
tests only in the `custom` folder of the current folder, and reads the config files of the current folder. Without
a `custom` folder only the built-in tests run.

Pester-format tests (`*.Tests.ps1`) must be in a `custom` folder: `-Path` itself, or a `custom` folder under it.
See [Pester-format tests](./pester-format-tests.md).

Maester matches the `custom` folder name without regard to case, so a `Custom` folder created by Maester 2.x keeps
working, and `New-MtTest` writes into it when it exists.

Rules for a test file:

- The file name is `Test.<ID>.ps1`, where `<ID>` is the `Id` in the attribute. The `.md` file has the same
  name with the `.md` extension and sits in the same folder. A custom test without its `.md` file is reported
  as `Error` with reason `InvalidMetadata`.
- The file contains exactly one function with a `[MaesterTest(...)]` attribute. It may contain other functions
  (helpers, or a family's instance source).
- At the top level the file contains only function definitions: no statements, no script-level `param()`
  block. Discovery never executes the file, and this rule keeps it that way.
- The test function has `[CmdletBinding()]`.

### Test IDs

An ID is letters and digits in segments separated by `.` or `-` (and `_` after the first segment). It starts
with a letter, contains at least one digit or separator, and is at most 64 characters. `CONTOSO.1001`,
`CONTOSO-ID-07` and `CT0001` are all valid. IDs are compared case-insensitively.

A test that implements a benchmark requirement is named after it: the suite's prefix, then the requirement's
ID as the benchmark writes it, without a version suffix. That is also its `Id` in the framework file. The prefix ends in a period;
the rest keeps the benchmark's own punctuation, so a reader can search for the ID the benchmark uses.

| Test ID | Prefix | The benchmark's ID |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CIS.M365.5.2.2.2` | `CIS.M365.` | Recommendation `5.2.2.2` of the CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark |
| `CISA.MS.AAD.3.1` | `CISA.` | SCuBA policy `MS.AAD.3.1v1`, without its version suffix |
| `ASD.ISM-1504` | `ASD.` | ISM control `ISM-1504`, written with a hyphen by ASD |
| `DISA.V-270233` | `DISA.` | Rule `V-270233` of a DISA STIG (vulnerability IDs are unique across STIGs) |

Use a prefix of your own. These prefixes belong to the tests that ship with Maester: `MT.`, `CISA.`, `CIS.`,
`EIDSCA.`, `ORCA.`, `AD-`, `AZDO.`, `ASD.`, `DISA.` and `MT1060.`. `MP.` is reserved for Maester Packs, third-party test packs
planned for a later release. A custom test with one of these prefixes still runs, with a
warning. A custom test that uses the exact ID of a built-in test is not run at all, and the built-in runs
instead. To change how a built-in test behaves, set its parameters or severity in the
[run configuration](../configuration/run-configuration.md), or copy it under your own ID and disable the
built-in.

Two native tests with the same ID (or the same function name) both get an `Error` row with reason
`DuplicateId`, and neither runs. When a native test and a Pester-format test share an ID, the native test
runs and the Pester test does not; it is listed under `Selection.Superseded` in the result with `MatchedBy`
`NativeTest`.

## What the function returns

| The function does | Result | Reason code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| returns `$true` | `Passed` | |
| returns `$false` | `Failed` | |
| calls `Add-MtTestResultDetail -Investigate` | `Investigate`, whatever it returns | |
| calls `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause <code>` | `Skipped`. The call ends the test. | `TestSkipped`, or `NotApplicable` for `-SkippedBecause NotApplicable` |
| calls `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Error`, or throws any error | `Error` | `TestError` |
| returns `$null` without skipping or `-Investigate` | `Skipped` | `NoResult` |
| returns something that is not a boolean, or more than one value | `Error` | `InvalidReturn` |
| runs longer than the configured timeout | `Error` | `Timeout` |

When several apply, they are evaluated in this order: `-SkippedBecause Error`, `-Investigate`, any other
skip, an uncaught error, the returned value.

Watch for stray output. A command whose output you do not capture (`$list.Add($x)` on an `ArrayList`, for
example) adds a second value to the function's output and turns the result into `InvalidReturn`. Assign such
calls to `$null` or pipe them to `Out-Null`.

### Add-MtTestResultDetail

[`Add-MtTestResultDetail`](../commands/Add-MtTestResultDetail.mdx) works as in 2.x. The parameters you use in a
native test:

- `-Result`: the Markdown result. It replaces `%TestResult%` in the `.md` file.
- `-GraphObjects` and `-GraphObjectType`: a list of objects rendered as a table with links to the admin
  portal, inserted where `%TestResult%` appears in `-Result`. See
  [Formatting test results](./formatting-test-results.md).
- `-Investigate`: the result needs a person to look at it.
- `-SkippedBecause`: skip the test for a reason only the test can see, such as `NotApplicable`,
  `NotSupportedAppPermission` or `Custom` with `-SkippedCustomReason`. Do not use the `NotConnected*` and
  `NotLicensed*` codes for conditions the attribute can declare; use `Service` and `License`.
- `-Description`: replaces the description from the `.md` file. Leave it out to use the `.md`.

`-TestTitle` and `-Severity` are ignored in a single-result native test: the title and severity come from the
attribute and the config. In a family, `-TestTitle` sets the instance's title when the instance object has no
`Title`. `-Severity` is used only when neither the config nor the attribute sets one.

### Embedding another tool's report

A test or a family's instance source that runs another tool can embed that tool's own single-file HTML report in
the Maester report with `Add-MtReportAttachment`:

```powershell
Add-MtReportAttachment -Name 'Zero Trust Assessment' -Path "$outputPath/ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html"
```

The report lists it near the bottom of the left menu (a pack's test's report goes in that pack's menu instead), and shows a button with that name on its overview page and
on the test's result (on every instance of a family). Each opens the embedded report in the main panel, beside the
Maester navigation, with a link to open it in a new browser tab. The attached report runs in a sandboxed frame
without access to the Maester report or its data. It works offline, so the Maester report stays one
file to share. The file is read and compressed at once, so you can delete the tool's output folder afterwards. The JSON
results file lists the attachment's name and size, not its content, and the HTML report leaves HTML attachments out
when `-RedactUserIdentity` is used.

With `-ContentType application/json`, an attachment is data for a view built into the report, which finds it by
its `Name` (the Zero Trust Assessment pack attaches its Zero Trust plan as `zero-trust-workshop`). It is not shown
as a button, and under `-RedactUserIdentity` it is redacted like the results instead of being left out.

### Errors and skips

Do not wrap the body in `try`/`catch` only to report `-SkippedBecause Error`. The engine runs every test inside
its own `try`, so any terminating error ends the test and becomes an `Error` row with the exception message as
`ReasonDetail` and the error record in `ErrorRecord`. Statement-terminating errors (a failed command, a method
call on `$null`) also end the test, so it cannot carry on with empty data and return `$true` by accident.

You may still use `try`/`catch` for a condition you handle, for example a 403 from Graph that you report as
`-SkippedBecause NotAuthorized`. A `-SkippedBecause` call made inside your own `try` block still skips the
test; the engine recognises the skip when your `catch` passes it to `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause
Error -SkippedError $_`.

Warnings and non-terminating errors written by the test are shown on the console and stored on the result row
in `Diagnostics`.

## Declare what the test needs

### Permission

`Permission` says what the identity Maester signs in with must be granted for the test to read its data. It
is recorded on the result row and in the catalog, so the docs and the report can say what to grant; Maester 3.0
does not skip a test on it.

Each permission is written `<Service>:<Kind>:<Name>`:

- **Service** is a name from the service registry (above) that the test also lists in `Service`.
- **Kind** is the kind of grant, from the list below.
- **Name** is the permission as the product spells it, for example `Policy.Read.All` or `View-Only Configuration`.
  It is everything after the second colon, so it may itself contain colons.

The test needs **every** element of the list. Inside an element, `|` joins **alternatives**: any one of them is
enough. Put the least privileged alternative first.

```powershell
Permission = 'Graph:Scope:Policy.Read.All'                                       # one permission
Permission = ('Graph:Scope:User.Read.All', 'Graph:Scope:AuditLog.Read.All')      # both
Permission = 'Graph:Scope:Policy.Read.All | Graph:Scope:Directory.Read.All'      # either
Permission = ('Graph:Scope:Policy.Read.All | Graph:Scope:Directory.Read.All',    # (either of these)
              'Graph:Scope:AuditLog.Read.All')                                   # and this
Permission = 'Graph:Scope:RoleManagement.Read.Directory | Graph:Role:Global Reader'  # a scope or a role
Permission = ('Graph:Scope:Policy.Read.All',                                     # two services: the test
              'ExchangeOnline:Role:View-Only Configuration')                     # lists both in Service
```

This is the other way round from `License`, where the list means "any one" and `&` means "all": a test usually
needs several permissions at once and has an alternative for only some of them. To say "(A and B) or C", write
"(A or C) and (B or C)": `('X:Scope:A | X:Scope:C', 'X:Scope:B | X:Scope:C')`.

| Service | Kind | Example name | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Graph` | `Scope` | `Policy.Read.All` | A Microsoft Graph permission that works as a delegated or an application permission |
| | `DelegatedScope` | `User.Read` | A Graph permission the test can use only delegated, with a user signed in |
| | `ApplicationScope` | `User.Read.All` | A Graph permission the test can use only as an application permission |
| | `Role` | `Global Reader` | A Microsoft Entra role, by its display name |
| `Azure` | `Role` | `Reader` | An Azure role; the scope it is assigned at is chosen at setup |
| | `Action` | `Microsoft.Authorization/policyAssignments/read` | An Azure resource provider operation |
| `ExchangeOnline` | `Role` | `View-Only Configuration` | An Exchange management role or role group, or an Entra role that grants one |
| | `Cmdlet` | `Get-OrganizationConfig` | A cmdlet the test runs |
| `SecurityCompliance` | `Role` | `View-Only DLP Compliance Management` | A Purview role or role group, or an Entra role that grants one |
| | `Cmdlet` | `Get-DlpCompliancePolicy` | A cmdlet the test runs |
| `SharePointOnline` | `Scope` | `Sites.FullControl.All` | A SharePoint API permission (not the Graph one of the same name) |
| | `Role` | `SharePoint Administrator` | A Microsoft Entra role |
| `Teams` | `Role` | `Teams Administrator` | A Microsoft Entra role |
| | `Cmdlet` | `Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy` | A cmdlet the test runs |
| `Dataverse` | `Role` | `System Administrator` | A Dataverse security role |
| `AzureDevOps` | `Scope` | `vso.project` | An OAuth or personal access token scope |
| | `Role` | `Project Collection Administrators` | A security group or access level |
| `GitHub` | `Permission` | `administration:read` | A GitHub App or fine-grained token permission |
| | `Scope` | `read:org` | A classic personal access token scope |
| | `Role` | `Organization owner` | An organization or enterprise role |
| `ActiveDirectory` | `Ldap` | `user:ReadProperty`, `*.ntSecurityDescriptor:ReadControl`, `Configuration/*:ReadProperty` | An LDAP right on an object class, `[<partition>/]<objectClass>[.<attribute>]:<right>`; the partition is `Configuration` or `Schema`, and the domain when omitted |
| | `Cim` | `root\MicrosoftDNS:MicrosoftDNS_Zone:Read` | Remote CIM (WMI) access, `<namespace>:<class>:<right>` |
| | `File` | `SYSVOL:Read` | A share on the domain controllers, `<share>:<right>` |
| | `Remoting` | `Microsoft.PowerShell` | A PowerShell remoting endpoint |
| | `Group` | `Remote Management Users` | Membership of a group |

The kinds are listed in `powershell/assets/MaesterServiceRegistry.psd1`. Maester writes a registered service
and kind in the registry's spelling and puts one space around each `|`. For a test shipped with Maester the
reader also checks that the service is one the test lists in `Service` and that the kind belongs to it; a custom
test may name a service or kind the registry does not know, such as a pack connector's.

Name the permission the test's code actually uses, the least privileged one that works. Do not list a
permission that a broader one in the same element already includes.

### TenantType and Cloud
## Parameters

A test's `param()` block lists the values a user can tune per tenant: thresholds, switches, objects to exclude.
Values come from the run configuration or from `Invoke-MtTest -Parameter`; a test always has to run with none
set, using its defaults.

```powershell
param(
    # Longest validity period, in days, that a certificate may be issued for.
    [ValidateRange(1, 3650)]
    [int] $MaximumValidityDays = 365,

    # Members of these groups are exempt from this check.
    [MaesterParameter(Kind = 'Entra.Group')]
    [string[]] $ExcludedGroups,

    # How strictly to evaluate.
    [ValidateSet('Strict', 'Lenient')]
    [string] $Mode = 'Strict'
)
```

Rules:

- Types are `int`, `bool`, `switch`, `string` or `string[]`, and `object[]` for a parameter bound to a setting
  that holds a list of objects.
- Names follow the [parameter naming rules](./attribute-rubric.md#parameter-names): `MaximumInactiveDays`,
  `ExcludedGroups`, `Strict`.
- Defaults are constants. No parameter is mandatory.
- Every parameter has a description: a `#` comment on the line directly above it, or `.PARAMETER` help. Only
  the comment line nearest the parameter is read, so keep the comment to one line or use `.PARAMETER`.
  `Get-MtTest` shows the description.
- Give thresholds a `ValidateRange`. A `ValidateSet` makes the parameter a list of choices.
- `Instance` and every name that starts with `Mt` belong to the engine and cannot be set.

Set values in the config:

```json
{
  "TestSettings": [
    { "Id": "CONTOSO.1002", "Parameters": { "ReasonMarker": "Off:" } },
    { "Id": "MT.1198", "Parameters": { "MaximumValidityDays": 180 } }
  ]
}
```

The engine checks each value against the `param()` block before the test runs. A name the test does not have,
a fraction for an `int`, a number for a `string`, a string for a `bool` or `switch`, or a value outside the
`ValidateRange` or `ValidateSet` gives that test an `Error` row with reason `InvalidConfiguration`; the run
carries on. A `string[]` parameter accepts one string or a list. The effective values, and where each came from
(`Default`, `Config`, `Setting` or `Parameter`), are written to the result row's `Parameters`.

### Values set once for many tests

Some values are the same for every test that needs them: the domains that never send email, the emergency access
accounts. An administrator sets these once in `GlobalSettings`, and a test receives one as a parameter bound to
the setting:

```powershell
param(
    # Domains that never send email.
    [MaesterParameter(Setting = 'ParkedDomains')]
    [string[]] $ParkedDomains = @()
)
```

```json
{
  "GlobalSettings": { "ParkedDomains": ["contoso-old.com"] },
  "TestSettings": [ { "Id": "CIS.M365.2.1.9", "Parameters": { "ParkedDomains": [] } } ]
}
```

The most specific value wins: `Invoke-MtTest -Parameter` or `Invoke-Maester -Parameter`, then the test's
`TestSettings` row, then `GlobalSettings`, then the parameter's default. A built-in setting must be registered in
`powershell/assets/MaesterSettings.psd1`, and the parameter's type must match it; the parameter takes the
setting's kind when it names none. A custom test or pack binds its own settings with a `Namespace.Key` name, such
as `Contoso.Regions`.

Maester checks `GlobalSettings` against the registry once, before the run: a value of the wrong type or one the
setting does not allow stops the run with one message, and a key it does not know is reported as a likely typo.
So give the parameter the same type, default and `ValidateSet` as the setting, and pass the value on to the
helpers that need it; a built-in test never calls `Get-MtSetting`. If another test calls yours as a
[shim](#tests-that-another-suite-already-has), it declares the same bound parameter and passes it on.

A test or helper that does call `Get-MtSetting`, as custom tests and packs may, has the name of each setting it
read recorded on its result (`SettingsRead`).

Bind a parameter only to a fact about the tenant or a choice the organisation makes once. A value a benchmark
sets stays a parameter of that test. Read [Parameters bound to a setting](./attribute-rubric.md#parameters-bound-to-a-setting)
before adding one.

### Parameter kinds

`[MaesterParameter(Kind = '...')]` says what a string parameter holds, so a user interface can offer a picker
and the engine can check the value's shape:

| Kind | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Entra.User` | User object ID |
| `Entra.Group` | Group object ID |
| `Entra.ServicePrincipal` | Service principal object ID |
| `Entra.Application` | Application object ID |
| `Entra.ConditionalAccessPolicy` | Conditional Access policy ID |
| `Entra.NamedLocation` | Named location ID |
| `Entra.Domain` | Domain name |
| `Entra.DirectoryRole` | Directory role definition ID |
| `Azure.Subscription` | Subscription ID |
| `Azure.ResourceGroup` | Resource group ID (`/subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/<name>`) |
| `Azure.Resource` | Azure resource ID |

A value that does not match the kind's pattern (for example a malformed GUID) is `InvalidConfiguration`. In the
config a value can be the ID itself or an object `{ "Id": "...", "DisplayName": "..." }`; the test always
receives the ID.

## Families: one test, several results
## Settings shared by many tests

Read tenant-wide settings from `GlobalSettings` in the config with `Get-MtSetting`:

```powershell
$accounts = Get-MtSetting -Name EmergencyAccessAccounts
$siteUrl  = Get-MtSetting -Name 'Contoso.SiteUrl' -Default 'https://contoso.sharepoint.com'
```

When the config does not set the value, `Get-MtSetting` returns Maester's default for the settings it knows,
else `-Default`. Use a `Namespace.Key` name for your own settings. Prefer a test parameter when the value
belongs to one test.

## What a custom test can call

Each custom test file is loaded into its own private module. It can call every command Maester exports,
including `Invoke-MtGraphRequest`, `Add-MtTestResultDetail`, `Get-MtSetting`, `Get-MtTenantContext`,
`Test-MtConnection`, `Get-MtLicenseInformation`, `Get-MtUser`, `Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy` and
`Invoke-MtTest`. It cannot call Maester's private functions, and it cannot replace a Maester command.

Functions defined in the same file are visible to the test. Functions in another test file are not. To share
code between files, put it in a helper `.ps1` (one that is not named `Test.*.ps1`) and dot-source it from
inside the test function: `. "$PSScriptRoot/Contoso.Helpers.ps1"`. `$PSScriptRoot` is the test file's folder.

To reuse a built-in check, run it through the engine instead of calling its function:

```powershell
$row = Invoke-MtTest -Id MT.1005
$row.Result   # Passed, Failed, Skipped, ...
```

The built-in check functions are no longer exported in 3.0, and they no longer contain their own connection
checks, so calling one directly is not supported.

## Running and inspecting tests

### Get-MtTest

`Get-MtTest` lists tests and their metadata without connecting to a tenant and without running any test code.

```powershell
Get-MtTest -Product entra -Feature conditional-access |
    Format-Table Id, Title, Severity                             # built-in tests
Get-MtTest MT.1198 | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Parameters    # a test's parameters
Get-MtTest -Path ./custom | Where-Object { -not $_.IsValid } |
    Select-Object Id, File, Errors                               # validate your own tests
```

Without `-Path` it returns the tests that ship with Maester. With `-Path` (a file or a folder) it reads and
validates those files; `IsValid` is `$false` and `Errors` lists every problem with its line number. `-Id`
accepts exact IDs and `*` wildcards. `-Product`, `-Feature`, `-Area`, `-Severity` and `-Suite` select by
attribute, as they do on `Invoke-Maester`, and `-Tag` matches what a run with that tag would select.

### Invoke-MtTest

`Invoke-MtTest` runs tests through the engine, with the same gates, parameter checks and result rows as
`Invoke-Maester`, and returns the rows. It writes no report.

```powershell
Invoke-MtTest -Path ./custom/Test.CONTOSO.1002.ps1
Invoke-MtTest -Path ./custom/Test.CONTOSO.1002.ps1 -Parameter @{ ReasonMarker = 'Off:' }
Invoke-MtTest -Path ./custom                       # every native test in the folder
Invoke-MtTest -Id MT.1005, 'CISA.MS.AAD.3.*'       # built-in tests
Invoke-MtTest -Path ./custom -Id CONTOSO.2001.abc  # one instance of a family
```

- `-Id` takes exact IDs or `*` wildcards. Without `-Path` it selects built-in tests; with `-Path` it selects
  among the tests in that file or folder. A family instance ID runs only that instance.
- `-Parameter` is allowed only when exactly one test is selected. Its values win over the config.
- `-Config` takes a path, an object or a list of them, as for `Invoke-Maester`. Without it, a test that calls
  `Invoke-MtTest` during an `Invoke-Maester` run uses the run's configuration; otherwise Maester reads the config
  files found from `-Path` (or the current folder).
- Tests you name run even if they are preview or long-running tests, and `Selection.DefaultAction` is
  ignored. A test disabled in the config is still `NotRun`.

Dot-sourcing a test file at the prompt defines the function but gives it no engine: no service checks, no
error handling and no `.md`. Use `Invoke-MtTest` while you write a test.

### Console output

`Invoke-Maester -Verbosity Normal` prints one line per finished native test with its result, ID, title and
duration, plus the first line of the reason for `Failed` and `Error`. `-Verbosity Detailed` also prints
`Running <ID>` when a test starts. The default, `None`, prints only the summary.

## Next steps

- [Formatting test results](./formatting-test-results.md)
- [Advanced guide](./advanced-concepts.md): `Invoke-MtGraphRequest`, caching and other helpers
- [Applicability and reason codes](../configuration/applicability.md)
- [Run configuration](../configuration/run-configuration.md)
- [Pester-format tests](./pester-format-tests.md)

For inspiration, see the community's [custom Maester tests](https://devclate.github.io/Custom-Maester-Tests/)
by Clayton Tyger (written for 2.x in Pester format; they still run, and `Convert-MtTest` can convert them).
