content.content:
### File organization

- One function per file, and the filename must match the function name exactly.
- Exported functions go in a group folder under `./powershell/public`, internal ones under `./powershell/internal`. See [Repository layout](#repository-layout) for which folder.
- Built-in security checks are native tests in `./tests/<suite>/[<service>/]Test.<ID>.ps1`, each with a `Test.<ID>.md` beside it. They are module source: the build defines their functions in the module.

### Pester Tests

- QA tests for the Maester module framework itself are at `./powershell/tests`. These are distinct from the bundled security test suites in `./tests`.
- When making changes to the module you can run the QA tests locally by running `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1`
- `pester.ps1` runs the test files in batches of eight, each batch in its own pwsh process, two processes at a time. Each process needs up to about 1.3 GB of memory. On a small VM use `-ThrottleLimit 1`; on a machine with memory to spare, `-ThrottleLimit 4` runs the suite in about half the time.
- While you work, run only the files that cover your change. `-Include` and `-Exclude` take file name patterns:

  ```powershell
  # The unit tests of the commands you changed
  ./powershell/tests/pester.ps1 -TestGeneral $false -Include 'Get-MtUser*', 'Test-MtCa*'

  # The checks that a new or changed native test must pass
  ./powershell/tests/pester.ps1 -TestFunctions $false -Include 'NativeTest*', 'RepositoryLayout*', 'MaesterTestTags*', 'LegacyIds*'

  # Everything except the slowest files, which regenerate the golden fixtures and the ORCA and EIDSCA tests
  ./powershell/tests/pester.ps1 -Exclude 'Golden*', 'GeneratedFileFormatting*', 'OrcaGenerator*', 'EidscaGenerator*'
  ```

- Run the whole suite once before you push, or let the pull request's build run it.
- On Windows, Microsoft Defender scans every script the module loads. If your policy allows it, excluding the folder of your clone from real-time scanning can make the run much faster.
- The **PSScriptAnalyzer**, **PSFramework** and **PSModuleDevelopment** modules are required to run the tests, install them with `Install-Module PSFramework, PSModuleDevelopment, PSScriptAnalyzer`
- The tests are run automatically on PRs and commits to the main branch and will fail if the tests do not pass

## Contributing new tests and updating existing tests

### Test folder convention

Every built-in check is a [native test](./writing-tests/index.mdx): `Test.<ID>.ps1` plus `Test.<ID>.md`, in the [tests](https://github.com/maester365/maester/tree/main/tests) folder of its suite:

- `/maester` - Maester tests (`MT.xxxx`), with a subfolder per service such as `/entra`, `/exchange`, `/teams`
- `/maester/xspm` - Exposure management tests (MT IDs, with their own suite)
- `/cisa` - CISA tests, with a subfolder per service
- `/cis` - CIS tests
- `/asd` - ASD Essential Eight and ISM tests (`ASD.ISM-xxxx`), with a subfolder per service
- `/disa` - DISA STIG tests (`DISA.V-xxxxxx`, named after the STIG rule), one folder for every product
- `/eidsca` - EIDSCA tests (generated, see below)
- `/orca` - ORCA tests (generated by `build/orca/Update-OrcaTests.ps1`)
- `/ad` - Active Directory tests
- `/custom` - Folder for users to add tests (do not add any tests to this folder).

Each suite folder has a `suite.json` with the suite's ID, name and source. Folder names follow the
[repository layout](#repository-layout).

A test says which requirement of a framework it implements in its attribute, `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'` or
`Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'` or `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'`. This is the same for a CIS, CISA or ASD
test and for a Maester test that checks what one of their requirements asks for.

The catalogue of each framework is a file beside the `suite.json` that declares it (`Frameworks`),
`frameworks/<key>.json`. It holds the name and version of the framework and every requirement with its facts: the
CIS level and profiles in `tests/cis/frameworks/`, the CISA criticality, upstream status and NIST SP 800-53
references in `tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json`, and the Essential Eight maturity level and strategy and the
ISM guideline, section and applicability in `tests/asd/frameworks/` (generated from the ISM OSCAL release by
`build/asd/Update-AsdFramework.ps1`). It does not list tests. The module build and the unit tests
fail when a `Control` names one of these frameworks and a requirement its file does not have, and when a test in
`tests/cis`, `tests/cisa` or `tests/asd` has no `Control` for its suite's framework.
See [Benchmarks and framework files](./writing-tests/index.mdx#benchmarks-and-framework-files) and
[Mapping a test to a framework](./writing-tests/index.mdx#mapping-a-test-to-a-framework).

### Checklist for writing good tests

When contributing tests, please ensure the following:

#### Before writing the test

- [x] Check if your new idea is not already covered by an existing test (you can also jump on the [Maester Discord](https://discord.entra.news) to discuss). `Get-MtTest` lists every test.
- [x] For a benchmark test (CIS, CISA, ASD), look for a test in any suite that reads the same setting, and read the benchmark's own audit or assessment guidance. If it asks for what that test checks, write a shim that returns that test's result instead of a second implementation; see [Tests that another suite already has](./writing-tests/index.mdx#tests-that-another-suite-already-has).
- [x] Reserve a unique id for your test. See [#️⃣ Pick next Maester test sequence number](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues/697) on how to reserve a unique id for your new test.

#### Writing the test

- [x] Scaffold the files in the right suite folder, for example `New-MtTest -Id MT.1234 -Title '...' -Service Graph -Product entra -Feature conditional-access -Area authentication -Path ./tests/maester/entra`, then follow [Writing native tests](./writing-tests/index.mdx).
- [x] Built-in tests must set `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `Mitre`, `Service` (or `None`) and `Author` (your GitHub handle) in the `[MaesterTest]` attribute, plus `UserImpact` and `ImplementationCost` unless `Severity` is `Info`, and describe every parameter. Choose the values with the [attribute rubric](./writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md), using keys from `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`. They are checked on the pull request; see [Attribute checks](#attribute-checks).
- [x] Do not add a `Tag` for the product, feature, area, suite, benchmark, licence or severity of a test, or for its ID: each of those has an attribute or is derived.
- [x] Do not check connections or licences in the test and do not wrap it in a `try`/`catch` that only reports `-SkippedBecause Error`: declare `Service` and `License` and let the engine handle it. The unit tests enforce this.
- [x] For a CIS, CISA or ASD test, set `Control` to the requirement it implements (`Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'`, `'cis-github:1.2.2'`, `'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'` or `'essential-eight:ISM-1504'`), and add the requirement to the framework file if it is new (`tests/cis/frameworks/cis-m365.json`, `tests/cis/frameworks/cis-github.json` or `tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json`): its `Id`, and its level and profiles or its criticality. The ASD files are generated from the ISM OSCAL release by `build/asd/Update-AsdFramework.ps1`, so a missing ISM control means the release has to be updated, not the file. Do not copy the benchmark's text into the file.
- [x] Tunable values (thresholds, objects to exclude) are parameters of the test function, not hard-coded.
- [x] The test's `.md` file explains the test in detail and provides all the context required for the user to resolve the issue, including deep links to the admin portal page to resolve the issue. This will be shown to the user when they view the test report. The file should include:
  - [x] Link to the admin portal blade where the setting can be configured
  - [x] A `#### Remediation action` section, and `<!--- Results --->` followed by `%TestResult%` at the end
  - [x] If there are multiple objects (e.g. list of CA policies, Users, etc) then use the `GraphObjects` and `GraphObjectType` parameters in [Add-MtTestResultDetail](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/public/Add-MtTestResultDetail.ps1). These include deep links to the admin portal. If the object type you wish is not available you can add it to [Get-GraphObjectMarkdown.ps1](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/internal/Get-GraphObjectMarkdown.ps1). Feel free to ask on Discord if you need help with this.
- [x] The test's page under `website/docs/tests/` is generated from the test files; do not write it by hand.
- [x] Check the test with `Get-MtTest <ID>` after `Import-Module ./powershell/Maester.psd1 -Force`, and run it with `Invoke-MtTest -Path <file>` against a tenant. `Get-MtTest -Path <file>` applies the rules of a custom test, so it does not report a missing attribute or a key that is not in the taxonomy.

When in doubt always check the existing tests for the conventions used, feel free to discuss on [Discord](https://discord.entra.news) or [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues).

#### Before creating the Pull Request

##### Test your code

- We run a bunch of pester tests on your code when a PR is raised and will block merge until the issues are addressed.
- Before you submit the PR, run the tests locally by running `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1`. See [Pester Tests](#pester-tests) for running a subset while you work.
- Fix any issues that are reported. If you need help see the `Common Pester test failures and how to fix` section below. Reach out on Discord if you need help.
- The **PSScriptAnalyzer**, **PSFramework** and **PSModuleDevelopment** modules are required to run the tests, install them with `Install-Module PSFramework, PSModuleDevelopment, PSScriptAnalyzer`
- If a test is not applicable (e.g. it says not to use plural but the product name is AzureDevOps then you can add a `SuppressMessageAttribute` tag (see Invoke-Maester.ps1 which has suppression tags at the beginning of the function).

### Attribute checks

A pull request that adds a test, or changes `Product`, `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost` or `Mitre` on an existing test, has those values checked against the [attribute rubric](./writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md) in two ways:

- The unit tests in [`NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1) fail when a built-in test misses a required attribute, uses a key that is not in the [taxonomy](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1), lists a retired or unknown ATT&CK technique, or carries a tag for something an attribute already says.

The test result now shows that 24 policies are failing the test but doesn't provide the names of the policies. To provide more context, you can add the names of the policies that are failing by passing the policies to the `Add-MtTestResultDetail` function.

![Test results showing graph objects](img/formatted-test-graph.png)

The `-GraphObjects` and `-GraphObjectType` parameters in `Add-MtTestResultDetail` allow you to pass objects to the test results and specify the type of object.

The test results can then display the names of the objects and also provide a deep link to the object in the Microsoft admin portal.

:::note
When using `-GraphObjects` the `-Result` string parameter needs to include `%TestResult%` at the position where the object names will be inserted.

The `%TestResult%` placeholder will be replaced with the names of the objects in the test results.
:::

The current list of supported object types includes Users, Groups, Devices, ConditionalAccess, AuthenticationMethod, AuthorizationPolicy, ConsentPolicy, Domains, IdentityProtection and UserRole.

Here's the updated test body with the graph objects that you can try out.

```powershell
    $policies = Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy
    $disabledWithoutReason = @($policies | Where-Object { $_.state -eq 'disabled' -and $_.displayName -notlike '*Disabled:*' })

    if ($disabledWithoutReason.Count -gt 0) {
        $result = "There are $($disabledWithoutReason.Count) disabled policies without a reason for being disabled.`n`n%TestResult%"
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $result -GraphObjects $disabledWithoutReason -GraphObjectType ConditionalAccess
    } else {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result 'Well done. All disabled policies have a reason for being disabled.'
    }
    return ($disabledWithoutReason.Count -eq 0)
```

To add support for additional types see [Add-MtTestResultDetail](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/public/run/Add-MtTestResultDetail.ps1) and [Get-GraphObjectMarkdown](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/internal/Get-GraphObjectMarkdown.ps1).

### Adding facts about an object

`-GraphObjects` says **which** objects a result is about: Maester lists them in the result, links them to the admin
portal and adds them to the report's **Affected objects** page with the check that named them.
[`Add-MtAffectedObjectFact`](../commands/Add-MtAffectedObjectFact.mdx) says **what is known** about an object: its last
sign-in, the permissions it holds, whether its secrets have expired. The facts appear with the object when its row on
the Affected objects page is expanded, whichever check named it.

| | `Add-MtTestResultDetail -GraphObjects` | `Add-MtAffectedObjectFact` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Answers | Which objects does this result concern? | What do we know about this object? |
| Adds an object to the Affected objects page | Yes | No: facts only describe objects a check already names |
| Shown | In the test result and on the Affected objects page | On the Affected objects page, in the JSON results and the objects files |

function Test-MtEmergencyAccessPhishingResistantMethod {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that every emergency access (break glass) account has a phishing-resistant authentication method registered.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Emergency access accounts are permanent Global Administrators that are excluded from Conditional Access, so
    the authentication method registered on the account is what protects it. Microsoft recommends a passkey
    (FIDO2) for these accounts: it cannot be phished or relayed by an adversary-in-the-middle proxy, and it
    satisfies the multifactor authentication that the Microsoft admin portals require.

    The accounts come from the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting. A configured group is expanded to its user
    members, nested groups included. For each account the test reads the registered authentication methods and
    passes when every account has at least one passkey (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business or platform
    credential method. The test is skipped when no emergency access accounts are configured.

    Certificate-based authentication is not registered on the user object, so an account that signs in only
    with a certificate fails this test.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtEmergencyAccessPhishingResistantMethod

    Returns true when every configured emergency access account has a phishing-resistant method registered.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/MT.1266
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id                 = 'MT.1266',
        Title              = 'Emergency access accounts should have a phishing-resistant authentication method registered.',
        Product            = 'entra',
        Feature            = 'authentication-methods',
        Area               = 'privileged-access',
        ResourceType       = 'User',
        Severity           = 'High',
        UserImpact         = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre              = ('T1078.004', 'T1566', 'T1557'),
        Control            = ('nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)', 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(8)'),
        Service            = 'Graph',
        Permission         = ('Graph:Scope:UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All', 'Graph:Scope:User.Read.All | Graph:Scope:Directory.Read.All', 'Graph:Scope:GroupMember.Read.All | Graph:Scope:Directory.Read.All'),
        Author             = 'your-github-handle'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Emergency access (break glass) accounts and groups, from the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting.
        [MaesterParameter(Setting = 'EmergencyAccessAccounts')]
        [object[]] $EmergencyAccessAccounts = @()
    )

    # The method types Microsoft Entra ID treats as phishing-resistant, with the name the result shows.
    $phishingResistantMethods = @{
        '#microsoft.graph.fido2AuthenticationMethod'                   = 'Passkey (FIDO2)'
        '#microsoft.graph.windowsHelloForBusinessAuthenticationMethod' = 'Windows Hello for Business'
        '#microsoft.graph.platformCredentialAuthenticationMethod'      = 'Platform credential'
    }

    # Throws when a configured account or group cannot be resolved, so the result is an error and not a pass.
    $configuredAccounts = @(Get-MtEmergencyAccessAccount -Account $EmergencyAccessAccounts | Where-Object { $_ })
    if ($configuredAccounts.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'No emergency access accounts are configured. Add your break glass accounts to the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting (GlobalSettings in maester-config.json) so this test can check them. See https://maester.dev/docs/configuration/emergency-access-accounts'
        return $null
    }

    # The user accounts to check: the configured users and the user members of the configured groups.
    $userNames = [ordered]@{}
    foreach ($account in $configuredAccounts) {
        if ($account.Type -eq 'group') {
            $members = @(Get-MtGroupMember -GroupId $account.ObjectId -Recursive | Where-Object { $_.'@odata.type' -eq '#microsoft.graph.user' })
            foreach ($member in $members) {
                $userNames[[string]$member.id] = $member.displayName
            }
        } else {
            $userNames[[string]$account.ObjectId] = $account.DisplayName
        }
    }

    if ($userNames.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'The groups in the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting have no user members, so there is no emergency access account to check.'
        return $null
    }

    $users = foreach ($userId in $userNames.Keys) {
        $registered = @((Get-MtUserAuthenticationMethod -UserId $userId).AuthenticationMethods | Where-Object { $_ })
        $methodNames = @($registered | ForEach-Object { $phishingResistantMethods[[string]$_.'@odata.type'] } | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Unique)
        [pscustomobject]@{
            id          = $userId
            displayName = if ($userNames[$userId]) { $userNames[$userId] } else { $userId }
            Methods     = $methodNames
        }
    }
    $users = @($users)
    $usersWithoutMethod = @($users | Where-Object { $_.Methods.Count -eq 0 })

    $portalLink = "$($__MtSession.AdminPortalUrl.Entra)#view/Microsoft_AAD_UsersAndTenants/UserProfileMenuBlade/~/UserAuthMethods/userId/{0}"
    $table = "| Emergency access account | Phishing-resistant methods | Status |`n| --- | --- | --- |`n"
    foreach ($user in $users) {
        $name = "[$(Get-MtSafeMarkdown $user.displayName)]($($portalLink -f $user.id))"
        if ($user.Methods.Count -gt 0) {
            $table += "| $name | $($user.Methods -join ', ') | ✅ Registered |`n"
        } else {
            $table += "| $name | None | ❌ Not registered |`n"
        }
    }

    if ($usersWithoutMethod.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Well done. Every emergency access account has a phishing-resistant authentication method registered.`n`n$table"
        return $true
    }

    $result = "These emergency access accounts have no phishing-resistant authentication method registered. Register a passkey (FIDO2) for each of them:`n`n%TestResult%`n`n$table"
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $result -GraphObjects $usersWithoutMethod -GraphObjectType Users
    return $false
}
EOF

            $members = @(Get-MtGroupMember -GroupId $account.ObjectId -Recursive | Where-Object { $_.'@odata.type' -eq '#microsoft.graph.user' })
            foreach ($member in $members) {
                $userNames[[string]$member.id] = $member.displayName
            }
        } else {
            $userNames[[string]$account.ObjectId] = $account.DisplayName
        }
    }

    if ($userNames.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'The groups in the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting have no user members, so there is no emergency access account to check.'
        return $null
    }

    $users = foreach ($userId in $userNames.Keys) {
        $registered = @((Get-MtUserAuthenticationMethod -UserId $userId).AuthenticationMethods | Where-Object { $_ })
        $methodNames = @($registered | ForEach-Object { $phishingResistantMethods[[string]$_.'@odata.type'] } | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Unique)
        [pscustomobject]@{
            id          = $userId
            displayName = if ($userNames[$userId]) { $userNames[$userId] } else { $userId }
            Methods     = $methodNames
        }
    }
    $users = @($users)
    $usersWithoutMethod = @($users | Where-Object { $_.Methods.Count -eq 0 })

    $portalLink = "$($__MtSession.AdminPortalUrl.Entra)#view/Microsoft_AAD_UsersAndTenants/UserProfileMenuBlade/~/UserAuthMethods/userId/{0}"
    $table = "| Emergency access account | Phishing-resistant methods | Status |`n| --- | --- | --- |`n"
    foreach ($user in $users) {
        $name = "[$(Get-MtSafeMarkdown $user.displayName)]($($portalLink -f $user.id))"
        if ($user.Methods.Count -gt 0) {
            $table += "| $name | $($user.Methods -join ', ') | ✅ Registered |`n"
        } else {
            $table += "| $name | None | ❌ Not registered |`n"
        }
    }

    if ($usersWithoutMethod.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Well done. Every emergency access account has a phishing-resistant authentication method registered.`n`n$table"
        return $true
    }

    $result = "These emergency access accounts have no phishing-resistant authentication method registered. Register a passkey (FIDO2) for each of them:`n`n%TestResult%`n`n$table"
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $result -GraphObjects $usersWithoutMethod -GraphObjectType Users
    return $false
}

input.content:
Every emergency access (break glass) account should have a phishing-resistant authentication method registered, such as a passkey on a FIDO2 security key.

Emergency access accounts are permanent Global Administrators, and they are excluded from Conditional Access so that a policy mistake or an outage cannot lock you out of the tenant. That exclusion also means no policy protects their sign-in: the authentication method registered on the account is the control. If the account has only a password, or a method such as a text message or an authenticator code, an attacker who phishes the credentials or relays the sign-in through an adversary-in-the-middle proxy signs in as a Global Administrator. A passkey is bound to the real sign-in page, so it cannot be phished or relayed. It also satisfies the multifactor authentication that the Microsoft admin portals require, so the account still works in an emergency.

Maester reads the accounts from the `EmergencyAccessAccounts` setting. A group in the setting is checked through its user members, including members of nested groups. The test passes when every account has at least one of these methods registered:

- Passkey (FIDO2), on a security key or in Microsoft Authenticator
- Windows Hello for Business
- Platform credential for macOS

The test is skipped when no emergency access accounts are configured. See [Emergency access accounts](https://maester.dev/docs/configuration/emergency-access-accounts) to tell Maester which accounts they are.

The test does not see certificate-based authentication, because a certificate is not registered on the user. If your emergency access accounts sign in only with a certificate, turn this test off in your configuration (`"Enabled": false` in its `TestSettings` row). It also does not check that weaker methods are absent or that the method is enforced at sign-in.

#### Remediation action

Microsoft recommends a passkey (FIDO2) on a security key for emergency access accounts, different from the method your everyday administrator accounts use.

1. In the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com), go to **Entra ID** > **Authentication methods** > **[Policies](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/AdminAuthMethods)**, open **Passkey (FIDO2)** and make sure it is enabled for the emergency access accounts.
2. Sign in as each emergency access account listed in the result, open [Security info](https://mysignins.microsoft.com/security-info), select **Add sign-in method** > **Security key** and follow the steps to register the key.
3. Confirm the key is listed under **Users** > the account > **Authentication methods**. The account names in the result link to that page.
4. Store each key in a secure place that more than one authorized administrator can reach, such as a safe, and test the sign-in at least every 90 days.

#### Related links

* [Manage emergency access admin accounts in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access)
* [Enable passkeys (FIDO2) for your organization](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-authentication-passkeys-fido2)

﻿<#
.SYNOPSIS
Reviews the rubric attributes of new and changed Maester tests with a reviewer model.

.DESCRIPTION
For every test that is new, or whose rubric attributes changed, this script sends the test's attribute values,
its source and its Markdown file to the Claude API together with the attribute rubric
(website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md) and the taxonomy (powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1), and
asks whether each value fits the rubric. It also sends the rubric attributes of the other tests under -Root with the
same Product and Feature, so that the model can hold the test to the same value as the same check in another suite. It writes attribute-review.json and attribute-review.md and returns:

    0  every reviewed attribute fits the rubric, or nothing needed review
    1  at least one attribute does not fit the rubric
    2  the review could not be completed (no API key, API error, refusal, unreadable file)

The files under review are treated as data. They are parsed with the PowerShell parser and never executed, and
the rubric, the taxonomy and the reviewer prompt are always read from -Root. In a pull request workflow -Root is
a checkout of the base branch and -HeadRoot holds the downloaded files of the pull request.

The API key is read from the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable.

.PARAMETER Root
The trusted repository root. The rubric, the taxonomy and the reviewer prompt are read from here.

.PARAMETER HeadRoot
The folder that holds the versions under review, laid out like the repository. Defaults to -Root.

.PARAMETER BaseRef
A git ref to compare with, for example origin/main. Used when -HeadRoot is the working tree. Without it, and with
-HeadRoot equal to -Root, every listed test is reviewed as new.

.PARAMETER File
Test files to consider, relative to the repository root (Test.<ID>.ps1 or Test.<ID>.md). When omitted and
-BaseRef is given, the files changed since that ref are used.

.PARAMETER OutputPath
Folder for attribute-review.json and attribute-review.md. Defaults to the current folder.

.PARAMETER Model
The Claude model to use.

﻿<#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Regenerates the Maester 2.x golden fixtures (tags and blocks, selection, config layouts).

    .DESCRIPTION
    Freezes today's (2.x) behaviour so later Maester 3.0 milestones can prove parity
    (design: docs/proposals/maester-3.0-design.md, sections 4, 7 and 15.2).

    Nothing here needs a tenant and no test body is executed:

    tags-and-blocks.json
        Every It in tests/**/*.Tests.ps1 (tests/Custom excluded), found by Pester discovery
        (Run.SkipRun = $true). For each It: Id, Name, Block, SelectionTags, ResultTags, File, Line.
          - Id and Block are computed exactly as ConvertTo-MtMaesterResult does (Id: text before the
            first colon after stripping the 'See https' suffix; Block: $test.Block.ExpandedName).
          - SelectionTags: the tags Pester filters on (tags of every ancestor Describe/Context plus the
            It tags), de-duplicated and sorted case-insensitively.
          - ResultTags: the Tag array ConvertTo-MtMaesterResult writes today,
            @($test.Block.Tag + $test.Tag | Select-Object -Unique). Only the immediate parent block's
            tags are included, so tests nested in a Context lose their Describe tags.
        A native test (every built-in test in 3.0) has one entry from the catalog: SelectionTags are the
        tags -Tag matches (the tags it carries, its ID and its 2.x tags from Maester.LegacyTags.json),
        ResultTags the tags its author wrote, and Block the name of its product. The committed file is
        the frozen 2.x snapshot; the golden test checks that every tag in it still selects the same tests.
        Its whose name is built at run time (an expandable string or a '<template>') are families
        (MT.1024, MT.1033, MT.1034, MT.1059, MT1060). They are recorded once, by literal ID prefix,
        with "Family": true, from the AST. Discovery-time tenant calls are neutralised by a stub
        module; any file whose discovery still fails falls back to an AST scan and is listed in _meta.

    selection.json

### `Test.MT.1266.ps1` (final)

```powershell
function Test-MtEmergencyAccessPhishingResistantMethod {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that every emergency access (break glass) account has a phishing-resistant authentication method registered.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Emergency access accounts are permanent Global Administrators that are excluded from Conditional Access, so
    the authentication method registered on the account is what protects it. Microsoft recommends a passkey
    (FIDO2) for these accounts: it cannot be phished or relayed by an adversary-in-the-middle proxy, and it
    satisfies the multifactor authentication that the Microsoft admin portals require.

    The accounts come from the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting. A configured group is expanded to its user
    members, nested groups included. For each account the test reads the registered authentication methods and
    passes when every account has at least one passkey (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business or platform
    credential method. The test is skipped when no emergency access accounts are configured.

    Certificate-based authentication is not registered on the user object, so an account that signs in only
    with a certificate fails this test.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtEmergencyAccessPhishingResistantMethod

    Returns true when every configured emergency access account has a phishing-resistant method registered.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/MT.1266
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id                 = 'MT.1266',
        Title              = 'Emergency access accounts should have a phishing-resistant authentication method registered.',
        Product            = 'entra',
        Feature            = 'authentication-methods',
        Area               = 'privileged-access',
        ResourceType       = 'User',
        Severity           = 'High',
        UserImpact         = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre              = ('T1078.004', 'T1566', 'T1557'),
        Control            = ('nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)', 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(8)'),
        Service            = 'Graph',
        Permission         = ('Graph:Scope:UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All', 'Graph:Scope:User.Read.All | Graph:Scope:Directory.Read.All', 'Graph:Scope:GroupMember.Read.All | Graph:Scope:Directory.Read.All'),
        Author             = 'merill'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Emergency access (break glass) accounts and groups, from the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting.
        [MaesterParameter(Setting = 'EmergencyAccessAccounts')]
        [object[]] $EmergencyAccessAccounts = @()
    )

    # The method types Microsoft Entra ID treats as phishing-resistant, with the name the result shows.
    $phishingResistantMethods = @{
        '#microsoft.graph.fido2AuthenticationMethod'                   = 'Passkey (FIDO2)'
        '#microsoft.graph.windowsHelloForBusinessAuthenticationMethod' = 'Windows Hello for Business'
        '#microsoft.graph.platformCredentialAuthenticationMethod'      = 'Platform credential'
    }

    # Throws when a configured account or group cannot be resolved, so the result is an error and not a pass.
    $configuredAccounts = @(Get-MtEmergencyAccessAccount -Account $EmergencyAccessAccounts | Where-Object { $_ })
    if ($configuredAccounts.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'No emergency access accounts are configured. Add your break glass accounts to the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting (GlobalSettings in maester-config.json) so this test can check them. See https://maester.dev/docs/configuration/emergency-access-accounts'
        return $null
    }

    # The user accounts to check: the configured users and the user members of the configured groups.
    $userNames = [ordered]@{}
    foreach ($account in $configuredAccounts) {
        if ($account.Type -eq 'group') {
            $members = @(Get-MtGroupMember -GroupId $account.ObjectId -Recursive | Where-Object { $_.'@odata.type' -eq '#microsoft.graph.user' })
            foreach ($member in $members) {
                $userNames[[string]$member.id] = $member.displayName
            }
        } else {
            $userNames[[string]$account.ObjectId] = $account.DisplayName
        }
    }

    if ($userNames.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'The groups in the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting have no user members, so there is no emergency access account to check.'
        return $null
    }

    $users = foreach ($userId in $userNames.Keys) {
        $registered = @((Get-MtUserAuthenticationMethod -UserId $userId).AuthenticationMethods | Where-Object { $_ })
        $methodNames = @($registered | ForEach-Object { $phishingResistantMethods[[string]$_.'@odata.type'] } | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Unique)
        [pscustomobject]@{
            id          = $userId
            displayName = if ($userNames[$userId]) { $userNames[$userId] } else { $userId }
            Methods     = $methodNames
        }
    }
    $users = @($users)
    $usersWithoutMethod = @($users | Where-Object { $_.Methods.Count -eq 0 })

    $portalLink = "$($__MtSession.AdminPortalUrl.Entra)#view/Microsoft_AAD_UsersAndTenants/UserProfileMenuBlade/~/UserAuthMethods/userId/{0}"
    $table = "| Emergency access account | Phishing-resistant methods | Status |`n| --- | --- | --- |`n"
    foreach ($user in $users) {
        $name = "[$(Get-MtSafeMarkdown $user.displayName)]($($portalLink -f $user.id))"
        if ($user.Methods.Count -gt 0) {
            $table += "| $name | $($user.Methods -join ', ') | ✅ Registered |`n"
        } else {
            $table += "| $name | None | ❌ Not registered |`n"
        }
    }

    if ($usersWithoutMethod.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Well done. Every emergency access account has a phishing-resistant authentication method registered.`n`n$table"
        return $true
    }

    $result = "These emergency access accounts have no phishing-resistant authentication method registered. Register a passkey (FIDO2) for each of them:`n`n%TestResult%`n`n$table"
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $result -GraphObjects $usersWithoutMethod -GraphObjectType Users
    return $false
}
```

### `Test.MT.1266.md` (final)

```markdown
Every emergency access (break glass) account should have a phishing-resistant authentication method registered, such as a passkey on a FIDO2 security key.

Emergency access accounts are permanent Global Administrators, and they are excluded from Conditional Access so that a policy mistake or an outage cannot lock you out of the tenant. That exclusion also means no policy protects their sign-in: the authentication method registered on the account is the control. If the account has only a password, or a method such as a text message or an authenticator code, an attacker who phishes the credentials or relays the sign-in through an adversary-in-the-middle proxy signs in as a Global Administrator. A passkey is bound to the real sign-in page, so it cannot be phished or relayed. It also satisfies the multifactor authentication that the Microsoft admin portals require, so the account still works in an emergency.

Maester reads the accounts from the `EmergencyAccessAccounts` setting. A group in the setting is checked through its user members, including members of nested groups. The test passes when every account has at least one of these methods registered:

- Passkey (FIDO2), on a security key or in Microsoft Authenticator
- Windows Hello for Business
- Platform credential for macOS

The test is skipped when no emergency access accounts are configured. See [Emergency access accounts](https://maester.dev/docs/configuration/emergency-access-accounts) to tell Maester which accounts they are.

The test does not see certificate-based authentication, because a certificate is not registered on the user. If your emergency access accounts sign in only with a certificate, turn this test off in your configuration (`"Enabled": false` in its `TestSettings` row). It also does not check that weaker methods are absent or that the method is enforced at sign-in.

#### Remediation action

Microsoft recommends a passkey (FIDO2) on a security key for emergency access accounts, different from the method your everyday administrator accounts use.

1. In the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com), go to **Entra ID** > **Authentication methods** > **[Policies](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/AdminAuthMethods)**, open **Passkey (FIDO2)** and make sure it is enabled for the emergency access accounts.
2. Sign in as each emergency access account listed in the result, open [Security info](https://mysignins.microsoft.com/security-info), select **Add sign-in method** > **Security key** and follow the steps to register the key.
3. Confirm the key is listed under **Users** > the account > **Authentication methods**. The account names in the result link to that page.
4. Store each key in a secure place that more than one authorized administrator can reach, such as a safe, and test the sign-in at least every 90 days.

#### Related links

* [Manage emergency access admin accounts in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access)
* [Enable passkeys (FIDO2) for your organization](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-authentication-passkeys-fido2)
* [Register a passkey using a FIDO2 security key](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-register-passkey-with-security-key)
* [Mandatory multifactor authentication for Azure and admin portals](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mandatory-multifactor-authentication)

<!--- Results --->
%TestResult%
```

## 2. What I read, in order, and what each told me

1. `CLAUDE.md` → `AGENTS.md`: two test trees, file location pattern, "no guards / no try-catch", the pointers to the skill, the guide and the rubric, the duplicate review, the attribute review, and the unit test command.
2. `.github/skills/maester-test-expert/SKILL.md` (read in full): the main source for almost everything.
3. `website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md` (in full).
4. `powershell/internal/services/entra/Get-MtEmergencyAccessAccount.ps1`, `powershell/assets/MaesterSettings.psd1`, `website/docs/configuration/emergency-access-accounts.md`.
5. Sibling tests: `MT.1034`, `MT.1005`, `MT.1191` (+ `.md`), `ASD.ISM-1649`, `MT.1063`, `MT.1067.md`.
6. `powershell/public/services/entra/Get-MtUserAuthenticationMethod.ps1`, `Get-MtUserAuthenticationMethodInfoByType.ps1`, `Get-MtGroupMember.ps1`.
7. `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx` (sections: files and layout, test IDs, return values, Permission, Parameters, settings, running tests).
8. `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`, `MaesterAttackTechniques.json`, `MaesterNistControls.json`, the CIS and CISA framework files, `Get-MtGraphScope.ps1`.
9. `website/docs/contributing.md` (Pester tests, checklist), `formatting-test-results.md`, `run-configuration.md` (how to disable a test).
10. Microsoft Learn (web): the emergency access accounts article and the Graph "List methods" reference, because the skill says to verify product facts there.

| Key thing | Source that told me |
| --- | --- |
| ID choice | SKILL.md workflow step 2 (issue #697, `Get-MtTest MT.12*`). I picked the next free ID locally: highest file is `MT.1265`, nothing in the repo mentions 1266. |
| File location | AGENTS.md "Repository layout" and SKILL.md "Anatomy of a Check": `tests/maester/entra/`. |
| Getting the break glass accounts | SKILL.md "Settings": a parameter bound with `[MaesterParameter(Setting = 'EmergencyAccessAccounts')]`, passed to `Get-MtEmergencyAccessAccount -Account`, never `Get-MtSetting`. The rubric's "Parameters bound to a setting" says the same. |
| Parameter naming | SKILL.md "Parameters" and the rubric's "Parameter names"; I reused the exact name and comment the other seven tests use. |
| Attribute values | The rubric, section by section. `Area = privileged-access` comes from its tie-break rule 1 and the area table naming "emergency access". `Severity = High` comes from "primary control … for privileged identities" with phishing sufficient. `ResourceType = User` because a failing result lists users. |
| "Don't fail when not configured" | No document says what to do. I copied `MT.1191`: `-SkippedBecause Custom` with a reason. |
| Validation steps | SKILL.md workflow steps 8–10 and the checklist; `contributing.md` for the targeted `pester.ps1 -Include` subsets. |

## 3. Gaps, ambiguities, contradictions and my guesses

**Found only because a validation step failed**
- **Golden fixtures.** Adding any built-in test fails `Golden.Tests.ps1` ("SelectedCount: 582, now 583"). Neither AGENTS.md, the skill nor the contributing checklist says a new test must regenerate `powershell/tests/fixtures/golden/selection.json`; only the failure message names `./build/golden/Export-MtGoldenFixture.ps1`. The contributing guide even suggests excluding `Golden*` while you work.
- **The regeneration has a side effect on macOS.** It also rewrote `config-layouts/root-custom-tenant/expected.json` (`Custom/` → `custom/` in a path). I reverted that file; Golden still passes locally with it reverted.
- **`FileEncoding.Tests.ps1` fails on a clean checkout**: `powershell/internal/engine/Test-MtGlobalSetting.ps1` has no BOM. It is not my file and I left it alone, so "pester.ps1 passes" is not achievable on this commit.

**Missing or ambiguous**
- **Not configured: which skip?** The skill says `NotApplicable` is for tenant state; "setting not configured" is neither that nor covered elsewhere. `MT.1005` falls back to auto-detection, `MT.1191` skips with `Custom`. I chose `Custom` with an actionable reason and no auto-detection.
- **`return $null` after a skip.** The skill says the skip call "ends the test", yet `MT.1191` writes `return $null` after it. I kept the return so the function also stops under a mock.
- **`New-MtTest` warns on the documented path.** The skill's own example (`New-MtTest -Id MT.1234 … -Path ./tests/maester/entra`) prints "The prefix of 'MT.1266' is reserved… Use your own prefix". It also names the function `Test-MT1266`, while the skill asks for a descriptive name, and writes no `Author` (the skill does mention that one).
- **Author handle.** Nothing says how to find the contributor's handle. I used `merill` from the git identity (`merill@merill.net`); change it if the contributor is someone else.
- **`Permission`.** Described in detail but optional, and only 1 of 95 Entra tests declares it. I declared it. The group-membership element is only needed when a group is configured, which the syntax cannot express.
- **Result table vs `-GraphObjects`.** The contributing checklist says to use `-GraphObjects` for lists of users; a per-user "which methods" table is not covered. I did both: failing users go through `-GraphObjects … Users`, and a table lists every account.
- **Which doc pages list tests that use a setting.** `emergency-access-accounts.md` has a "Related Tests" table with only `MT.1005`, though seven tests bind the setting. No guidance says to maintain it. I added my row only.
- **Unit test for a check.** Some checks have one in `powershell/tests/functions/`, most do not, and the guidance is silent. I added one.
- **`./module` build output.** `Build-MaesterModule.ps1` refuses an output folder outside the repo; the default `./module` leaves `git status` clean.

**Contradictions**
- `index.mdx` "Settings shared by many tests" shows `Get-MtSetting -Name EmergencyAccessAccounts` as the way to read the setting, while the skill, the rubric and the "Values set once for many tests" section of the same page say a built-in test never calls it. The first section is written for custom tests but does not say so.
- `MaesterSettings.psd1` describes the setting as accounts "excluded from Conditional Access checks", which no longer covers every test that binds it. I did not change it.
- Sibling emergency-access tests all have `Mitre = 'None'` and the Feature of where they are fixed; the skill says not to copy neighbours, so my values differ from theirs by design.

**Judgement calls worth a reviewer's eye**
- **What counts as phishing-resistant:** FIDO2/passkey, Windows Hello for Business and platform credential. Microsoft's emergency access article recommends only passkey (FIDO2) or certificate-based authentication. Certificate-based authentication is not visible on the user, so a CBA-only account fails; the `.md` says to disable the test in that case. I did not add a parameter for the accepted methods.
- **Registration, not enforcement.** The test does not check that weaker methods are absent. The `.md` says so. This makes `Severity = High` and the three ATT&CK techniques arguable.
- **`ImplementationCost = Low`** over Medium, using the rubric's "choose the lower" rule; buying hardware keys could justify Medium.

### `Test.MT.1266.ps1` (final)

```powershell
function Test-MtEmergencyAccessPhishingResistantMethod {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that every emergency access (break glass) account has a phishing-resistant authentication method registered.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Emergency access accounts are permanent Global Administrators that are excluded from Conditional Access, so
    the authentication method registered on the account is what protects it. Microsoft recommends a passkey
    (FIDO2) for these accounts: it cannot be phished or relayed by an adversary-in-the-middle proxy, and it
    satisfies the multifactor authentication that the Microsoft admin portals require.

    The accounts come from the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting. A configured group is expanded to its user
    members, nested groups included. For each account the test reads the registered authentication methods and
    passes when every account has at least one passkey (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business or platform
    credential method. The test is skipped when no emergency access accounts are configured.

    Certificate-based authentication is not registered on the user object, so an account that signs in only
    with a certificate fails this test.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtEmergencyAccessPhishingResistantMethod

    Returns true when every configured emergency access account has a phishing-resistant method registered.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/MT.1266
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id                 = 'MT.1266',
        Title              = 'Emergency access accounts should have a phishing-resistant authentication method registered.',
        Product            = 'entra',
        Feature            = 'authentication-methods',
        Area               = 'privileged-access',
        ResourceType       = 'User',
        Severity           = 'High',
        UserImpact         = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre              = ('T1078.004', 'T1566', 'T1557'),
        Control            = ('nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)', 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(8)'),
        Service            = 'Graph',
        Permission         = ('Graph:Scope:UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All', 'Graph:Scope:User.Read.All | Graph:Scope:Directory.Read.All', 'Graph:Scope:GroupMember.Read.All | Graph:Scope:Directory.Read.All'),
        Author             = 'merill'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Emergency access (break glass) accounts and groups, from the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting.
        [MaesterParameter(Setting = 'EmergencyAccessAccounts')]
        [object[]] $EmergencyAccessAccounts = @()
    )

    # The method types Microsoft Entra ID treats as phishing-resistant, with the name the result shows.
    $phishingResistantMethods = @{
        '#microsoft.graph.fido2AuthenticationMethod'                   = 'Passkey (FIDO2)'
        '#microsoft.graph.windowsHelloForBusinessAuthenticationMethod' = 'Windows Hello for Business'
        '#microsoft.graph.platformCredentialAuthenticationMethod'      = 'Platform credential'
    }

    # Throws when a configured account or group cannot be resolved, so the result is an error and not a pass.
    $configuredAccounts = @(Get-MtEmergencyAccessAccount -Account $EmergencyAccessAccounts | Where-Object { $_ })
    if ($configuredAccounts.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'No emergency access accounts are configured. Add your break glass accounts to the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting (GlobalSettings in maester-config.json) so this test can check them. See https://maester.dev/docs/configuration/emergency-access-accounts'
        return $null
    }

    # The user accounts to check: the configured users and the user members of the configured groups.
    $userNames = [ordered]@{}
    foreach ($account in $configuredAccounts) {
        if ($account.Type -eq 'group') {
            $members = @(Get-MtGroupMember -GroupId $account.ObjectId -Recursive | Where-Object { $_.'@odata.type' -eq '#microsoft.graph.user' })
            foreach ($member in $members) {
                $userNames[[string]$member.id] = $member.displayName
            }
        } else {
            $userNames[[string]$account.ObjectId] = $account.DisplayName
        }
    }

    if ($userNames.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'The groups in the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting have no user members, so there is no emergency access account to check.'
        return $null
    }

    $users = foreach ($userId in $userNames.Keys) {
        $registered = @((Get-MtUserAuthenticationMethod -UserId $userId).AuthenticationMethods | Where-Object { $_ })
        $methodNames = @($registered | ForEach-Object { $phishingResistantMethods[[string]$_.'@odata.type'] } | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Unique)
        [pscustomobject]@{
            id          = $userId
            displayName = if ($userNames[$userId]) { $userNames[$userId] } else { $userId }
            Methods     = $methodNames
        }
    }
    $users = @($users)
    $usersWithoutMethod = @($users | Where-Object { $_.Methods.Count -eq 0 })

    $portalLink = "$($__MtSession.AdminPortalUrl.Entra)#view/Microsoft_AAD_UsersAndTenants/UserProfileMenuBlade/~/UserAuthMethods/userId/{0}"
    $table = "| Emergency access account | Phishing-resistant methods | Status |`n| --- | --- | --- |`n"
    foreach ($user in $users) {
        $name = "[$(Get-MtSafeMarkdown $user.displayName)]($($portalLink -f $user.id))"
        if ($user.Methods.Count -gt 0) {
            $table += "| $name | $($user.Methods -join ', ') | ✅ Registered |`n"
        } else {
            $table += "| $name | None | ❌ Not registered |`n"
        }
    }

    if ($usersWithoutMethod.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Well done. Every emergency access account has a phishing-resistant authentication method registered.`n`n$table"
        return $true
    }

    $result = "These emergency access accounts have no phishing-resistant authentication method registered. Register a passkey (FIDO2) for each of them:`n`n%TestResult%`n`n$table"
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $result -GraphObjects $usersWithoutMethod -GraphObjectType Users
    return $false
}
```

### `Test.MT.1266.md` (final)

```markdown
Every emergency access (break glass) account should have a phishing-resistant authentication method registered, such as a passkey on a FIDO2 security key.

Emergency access accounts are permanent Global Administrators, and they are excluded from Conditional Access so that a policy mistake or an outage cannot lock you out of the tenant. That exclusion also means no policy protects their sign-in: the authentication method registered on the account is the control. If the account has only a password, or a method such as a text message or an authenticator code, an attacker who phishes the credentials or relays the sign-in through an adversary-in-the-middle proxy signs in as a Global Administrator. A passkey is bound to the real sign-in page, so it cannot be phished or relayed. It also satisfies the multifactor authentication that the Microsoft admin portals require, so the account still works in an emergency.

Maester reads the accounts from the `EmergencyAccessAccounts` setting. A group in the setting is checked through its user members, including members of nested groups. The test passes when every account has at least one of these methods registered:

- Passkey (FIDO2), on a security key or in Microsoft Authenticator
- Windows Hello for Business
- Platform credential for macOS

The test is skipped when no emergency access accounts are configured. See [Emergency access accounts](https://maester.dev/docs/configuration/emergency-access-accounts) to tell Maester which accounts they are.

The test does not see certificate-based authentication, because a certificate is not registered on the user. If your emergency access accounts sign in only with a certificate, turn this test off in your configuration (`"Enabled": false` in its `TestSettings` row). It also does not check that weaker methods are absent or that the method is enforced at sign-in.

#### Remediation action

Microsoft recommends a passkey (FIDO2) on a security key for emergency access accounts, different from the method your everyday administrator accounts use.

1. In the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com), go to **Entra ID** > **Authentication methods** > **[Policies](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/AdminAuthMethods)**, open **Passkey (FIDO2)** and make sure it is enabled for the emergency access accounts.
2. Sign in as each emergency access account listed in the result, open [Security info](https://mysignins.microsoft.com/security-info), select **Add sign-in method** > **Security key** and follow the steps to register the key.
3. Confirm the key is listed under **Users** > the account > **Authentication methods**. The account names in the result link to that page.
4. Store each key in a secure place that more than one authorized administrator can reach, such as a safe, and test the sign-in at least every 90 days.

#### Related links

* [Manage emergency access admin accounts in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access)
* [Enable passkeys (FIDO2) for your organization](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-authentication-passkeys-fido2)
* [Register a passkey using a FIDO2 security key](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-register-passkey-with-security-key)
* [Mandatory multifactor authentication for Azure and admin portals](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mandatory-multifactor-authentication)
```
